articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Should Steelers be worried after embarrassing blowout loss?
articles.summary: The Steelers were run off the field by the Bengals on Sunday night.
articles.body:
One bad game shouldn't eliminate eight games of solid football.

But that was a seriously bad game for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Get out-gained 337-40 in a half and there will be some reasons for concern. The Steelers were absolutely blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals, and it didn't help that it happened on a big Sunday night stage. The Steelers were 6-2 going into the game and while there was skepticism over their staying power, nobody expected them to get destroyed like that.

The Steelers don't seem too worried about it ruining their season. Aaron Rodgers handled a question about whether the loss would change the trajectory of the season with, "That's very dramatic," and head coach Mike McCarthy took a similar tack.

"It's one loss and it will be dealt with as such," McCarthy said, via the team's site . "I'm more focused on the details of the fundamentals and the things we needed to do. We're not going to drive down the drama road. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy. We're going to pour our energy into ourselves, look in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control."

That's a fine approach, because there's nothing else McCarthy can say. But the Steelers have some real concerns. They came into the season tied for the oldest roster in the NFL, with many older veterans starting with 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It's a long season and the Steelers have to worry about injury and fatigue setting in. The Steelers have gotten very little out of their receivers this season, which limits the explosiveness of the offense, and while the defense has been good it was picked apart by Joe Burrow.

But it's not time to get too worried. The Steelers had shown significant improvement before having a horrendous night in Cincinnati. That isn't all erased, nor are six wins in what is becoming a very soft AFC wild-card race. Rodgers was good enough with the limitations at receiver through eight games and while Sunday night started with him throwing incomplete on his first seven passes for the first time in his career, there haven't been signs of a steep decline before Sunday night. It could happen in the second half of the season but there's no clear and imminent danger of it.

Good teams can have bad games. The Bengals are hot. It happens. As McCarthy said, there's no reason to go down a drama road. The Steelers should be fine. But that's a little less certain after a truly miserable night in Cincinnati.

Panic meter: Let's not give up on the Steelers yet, but remember Sunday night as a turning point if things do go south.

When Drake Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson, Patriots and Lions fans had no idea both teams' seasons were changing on that play.

The Patriots are concerned that Maye fractured his ankle, and we'll get to Hutchinson in a bit. It appears Maye is either going to miss significant time or the rest of the season. That's terrible news for the 5-5 Patriots less than a week after the trade deadline passed. Jimmy Garoppolo's name has been thrown around but realistically, it's hard to find any quarterback who is still unsigned in mid-November to save the season.

Former Patriots quarterback Matt Cassel, who is 44 years old, had some jokes.

It might not be that much worse than Tommy DeVito, who was awful in relief of Maye. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts. The Patriots had 91 yards on 11 possessions after Maye's injury. It was unwatchable football. And that's likely to be the case for the rest of the season.

Panic meter: Hey Patriots fans, at least the Celtics and Bruins are good.

Aidan Hutchinson was excited for a third-down sack on Drake Maye, so he jumped up and the landing might have ruined the Lions' Super Bowl hopes.

Hutchinson tore his ACL on the celebration, a brutal injury for Hutchinson and Detroit as well. Detroit was already without standout linebacker Jack Campbell. Hutchinson's knee injury removes the two best players from a defense that wasn't very good with them.

The Lions are 7-2 and Detroit fans will point to 2024, when the team went 15-2 after Hutchinson broke his leg. Perhaps they can get on a roll while being shorthanded. But realistically and unfortunately, the ceiling for the Lions was lowered with the injury.

Panic meter: The Lions shouldn't fall apart, but that celebration was a turning point in their season.

Everyone will have issues with the Vikings' blitz-happy defense this season. The Packers certainly have. They allowed eight sacks on Sunday and 12 in two meetings against the Vikings. While that's certainly too many, Green Bay has allowed only 13 sacks in their other eight games.

The problem is that the next opponent, after the bye, is Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and the Rams. There's a lot of work to be done before that game the day before Thanksgiving.

The Packers lost 30-10 to the Vikings and they obviously haven't matched up well with Minnesota this season. But Green Bay was playing very well before Sunday's game and are still in fine shape in the NFC wild-card race.

Panic meter: As long as Brian Flores isn't on the other sideline, Green Bay should be fine.

The Texans' season can be viewed in an optimistic way, if you wish. Five of their losses this season have come on a drive by the opponent in the final minutes of regulation or in overtime. Close games like that should be close to 50/50 propositions, so with just a little more luck Houston would be right in the playoff picture.

But maybe it's not just luck. The Texans' defense, which was supposed to be good this season, has failed repeatedly when asked to close out a game. And regardless of how the Texans got to 3-6, that's where they are. And they have lost a key tiebreaker to the Browns, who are currently the No. 7 seed in the AFC.

Houston's playoff odds are 34.4% via DVOA , which seems high for a team three games under .500. That's because the AFC's wild-card race isn't very good. But, maybe the Texans aren't very good either.

Panic meter: The talent is still there, but the season is slipping away fast with bad losses.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes’ women's sports vision pays off as Patrick Mahomes’ Kansas City Current investment soars to $325 million
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations, and Brittany Mahomes helped build that number.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations, and Brittany Mahomes helped build that number. The club ranks second in the league, behind only Angel City FC at $340 million. Kansas City's value rose from $275 million a year earlier, a jump of $50 million, or about 18 percent. Patrick Mahomes joined his wife as a co-owner in 2023, but the idea began with her. She was among the founding owners in 2020, when the team had no history, no stadium and no wins to point to.Brittany Mahomes' women's sports vision is paying off for the CurrentBrittany Mahomes played forward at the University of Texas at Tyler from 2013 to 2016 and later played professionally in Iceland. She retired from the game in 2017 and moved to Kansas City to be with Patrick. Three years later, she became a founding owner of a new NWSL club in her adopted city. The bet was that a town that packs Arrowhead every fall could fill a soccer stadium for women, too.It did not look smart at first. The Current finished last in the league in 2021, their opening season, and nobody was calling the owners visionaries yet.The climb since has been steep. Forbes had the club near $75 million in 2024, then at $275 million in 2025, and now at $325 million. Put another way, the club's value has more than quadrupled in two years. Revenue backs it up. The Current reported $36 million in annual revenue in last year's Forbes figures, the most of any team in the league.Patrick's part is real, though it came later. In January 2023 he became the first active NFL player to hold a stake in an NWSL club, joining Brittany and co-owners Angie and Chris Long. Brittany, though, is the one who started it. He has spent much of this year recovering from injuries, so the valuation has been a welcome piece of news away from football.Where the Current stand against the rest of the NWSLThe $15 million gap to Angel City FC is small, but the two clubs got here differently. Angel City plays in Los Angeles, with a big media market and celebrity investors. Kansas City is a smaller market and has built its case on revenue and a stadium made for the team.Twelve months, $50 million. That is a lot of value added in a year by a team that played its first game in 2021. Growth at that pace usually raises expectations for crowds, results and a stronger roster.Other NFL owners have noticed. Families like the Haslams and Arthur Blank have since moved into the league, which backs up the early call Brittany made in 2020. Their arrival suggests the league's top-end value is no longer a Los Angeles story alone.Still, a valuation is a number on a list, and the Current know it. The club's 2021 finish showed that money and results do not always move together. A $325 million team is now expected to compete for trophies, and the owners have said from the start they want to do right by the players and the city. Fans will judge that on the pitch, not in a Forbes table.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Drake Maye injury update: How long could Patriots QB be out and what his recovery timeline might look like
articles.summary: Drake Maye is unlikely to start for the Patriots after the bye, and the injury may be worse than a sprain.
articles.body: Drake Maye is unlikely to start for the Patriots after the bye, and the injury may be worse than a sprain. The quarterback hurt his right ankle on New England’s opening drive of a 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday. He never came back. ESPN reported the team fears a fracture, and coach Mike Vrabel said Monday he doesn’t see Maye ready for the Week 12 trip to the Chargers. Maye had started 42 straight games. The diagnosis now decides how much of this season he keeps.Drake Maye injury timeline after the Lions lossDrake Maye went down on a third-and-goal sack by Aidan Hutchinson. The Lions pass rusher wrapped him up and rolled onto the back of his lower legs. Maye limped to the sideline, then to the locker room. The Patriots listed him as questionable, then ruled him out, and Tommy DeVito finished the game.The early read was a sprain.Dr. David Chao, a former Chargers team physician, watched the replay and wrote, “By video, mild right high ankle sprain.” A mild one usually costs two to four weeks. Chao also warned the bye week wouldn’t be enough. “This is likely a multi-week injury still,” he said.Then the story shifted. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the Patriots fear Maye fractured the ankle, which could require surgery, and sources told ESPN the injury could end his season. Maye stayed in Germany for more tests before heading home. Vrabel kept his answer short on Monday. “I wouldn’t imagine him being available coming out of the bye,” he said.Dr. Atsushi Endo, an orthopedic surgeon at Tufts Medical Center, gave WCVB a wide range for a sprain. “If Maye suffered a high ankle sprain, where the ligament between the two shin bones are injured, that could take anywhere from 2 to 6 weeks. If the injury is unstable, it could take two months or longer,” Endo said.The Patriots haven’t announced a diagnosis.What a longer absence would do to New England Patriots?A fracture changes the math. The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons says most ankle fractures need at least six weeks just for early healing, and full bone healing generally takes 10 to 12 weeks. Surgery would stretch that further. Even so, the type and location of a break matter, so the word “fracture” alone doesn’t set a return date.Injured reserve is the other marker to watch. Chao hoped Maye could avoid it, but a stint there means at least four missed games. For a quarterback who hadn’t missed one as a pro, that is new ground.The timing is awkward. New England was 5-4 and coming off a 45-27 loss to Green Bay before Munich, and the bye gives the staff one week to regroup. Vrabel’s comments point to DeVito getting the Chargers start on Nov. 29. Maye came into Sunday with 2,282 passing yards, 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, so the offense built around him will have to change shape fast.The Patriots come out of the bye with a roster call hanging over them: hold Maye’s spot, or move him to injured reserve.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany reveal whether baby No. 4 will give Sterling and Bronze another brother or sister
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are expecting another boy.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are expecting another boy. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and his wife revealed the gender of their fourth child on November 17, a week after announcing the pregnancy. The new arrival will give their family two boys and two girls, joining Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 21 months. The couple shared the news through a gender reveal video on Instagram, with all three children present. It also fulfilled Patrick's earlier wish to have another son alongside Bronze.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany are expecting another boyThe couple chose a cake reveal to share the news with family and friends. In their joint Instagram video, Patrick and Brittany each pulled a champagne glass from a cake. Blue filling inside the cake confirmed they were having a boy, while matching confetti cannons added to the celebration.Their children watched as the reveal unfolded. Patrick and Brittany embraced before turning their attention to Sterling, Bronze and Golden, showering them with hugs and kisses. The couple captioned the post "Baby #4," while Patrick added three blue heart emojis in the comments.The announcement also brought a playful comment from Patrick's earlier remarks into focus. During a press conference on November 11, the Chiefs quarterback had admitted that he was hoping for another boy. He already has Bronze at home and had joked about balancing the numbers between the boys and girls.“Obviously it’s a blessing to have another baby on the way. I’m excited for it,” Patrick said. “I’m hoping that me and Bronze can even up the score.”He also made clear that the baby's health mattered more than the gender. “But I’m just praying for a healthy baby at the end of the day,” he said.The couple had first announced the pregnancy on November 10. They posted a photograph of their three children placing their hands on Brittany's baby bump, alongside the caption, “Another blessing from God. & then there were 6.”Patrick and Brittany have spoken about how parenthood changed themThe fourth pregnancy marks another chapter for the couple, who have been together since high school and married for four years. Their family life has also shaped how both approach their responsibilities away from football and public appearances.Brittany has spoken about becoming more selective with her time since having children. In a July interview with Yahoo Entertainment, she explained how motherhood changed her priorities."When you become a mom, you learn to say no to things that aren't as important and focus on what's best for your life and your family," she said. "Keeping my eyes and my mind and my focus on my family and the things that matter the most."Patrick has also discussed the lessons fatherhood has taught him, particularly patience and the need to encourage his children. Ahead of the 2024 Super Bowl, he told reporters that building confidence was an important part of raising them."You learn how to try to really boost people’s confidence, especially your kids,” he shared, per KSL Sports. “Through seasons like I’ve had this last year, it’s never losing hope, never going too negative in adverse times. Just continue to boost people’s confidence, continue to strive for hard work and really be patient."With another son on the way, Patrick's wish has come true. The Mahomes household will soon have two boys and two girls, and Sterling, Bronze and Golden will have a new sibling to welcome.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "I love you Boys to death. But...": Post Malone can no longer hide his frustration as Dallas Cowboys’ latest loss pushes him over the edge
articles.summary: Post Malone has seen enough. The singer posted a heated message on X after the Dallas Cowboys lost 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov.
articles.body: Post Malone has seen enough. The singer posted a heated message on X after the Dallas Cowboys lost 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 15, at AT&T Stadium. Dallas gave up a franchise-record 584 yards, even though Dak Prescott threw five touchdowns. Malone, a Cowboys fan since childhood, called the defense out of control and asked the team to fix it. He still ended the post with love for the players. It was a blunt message from one of the team’s loudest supporters, and his patience clearly has limits.Post Malone calls out Cowboys after 49ers lossMalone took to X after the game, and he skipped the polite version. He opened with the defense.“600 yards allowed is out of control. With the amount of studs we have on this team, there is no reason to keep losin EVERY [expletive] SUNDAY,” he wrote. The real figure was 584, close enough that no fan will quibble.He kept going, and he did not name a single player. “I love you Boys to death. But we gotta fix this [expletive]. Don’t give up fellas @dallascowboys,” he continued. Then came the sign-off. “p.s. if you’re readin this I love YOU too.”That mix is what makes the post work. Anger is easy. Staying loyal while you rage is harder, and it sounds like every fan who has yelled at a TV on a bad Sunday.That is the odd part of this loss. Prescott’s five touchdowns and 40 points would win most days. Instead, the defense turned a shootout into a record night for the other side.Why the Cowboys mean so much to himMalone was born Austin Richard Post in Syracuse, New York. He moved to Grapevine, Texas, at age 9 because his father, Rich Post, landed a job overseeing concessions for the Cowboys. Some days, young Austin slept on a cot at Texas Stadium while his dad worked.The 31-year-old has since become one of the most recognizable Cowboys fans anywhere. He has brought that history into his work. In 2023, he released a limited-edition Cowboys apparel collection and teamed up with Raising Cane’s on a Cowboys-themed restaurant in Dallas. When his tour stopped at AT&T Stadium in May 2025, he wore kicker Brandon Aubrey’s No. 17 jersey.The big stages followed. He sang “America the Beautiful” before Super Bowl LVIII in February 2024 and joined Beyoncé as a surprise guest at her Christmas Day halftime show that December. Then came Thanksgiving 2025, when he headlined the Cowboys’ halftime show against the Chiefs. “I’m from Texas. I grew up a Cowboys fan and have been watching this halftime show for years,” Malone said when the performance was announced. For the kid from the cot, it was a real homecoming.Nearly a year on, the view from his seat is rougher. Sunday’s game made that clear. He is still all in, but he wants a defense worth cheering for.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ciara has one request before welcoming baby No. 5 as Russell Wilson gets ready for another life-changing moment: ‘It’s Time’ for the Baby ‘Train to Slow Down’
articles.summary: Ciara and Russell Wilson are expecting their fifth child, and the singer says the pregnancy is going well.
articles.body: Ciara and Russell Wilson are expecting their fifth child, and the singer says the pregnancy is going well. The 41-year-old gave PEOPLE an update at Macy’s Santaland Premiere in New York City on Thursday, Nov. 12. The couple announced the news on Sept. 6, 2026, with a short social media post. Their message read “One more person to Love 🖐🏽🥺🖤.” Two months later, Ciara says she has to slow down at certain points in the day. Wilson, 37, joked about how often the family grows, and she had a quick reply ready.Ciara says it is time for the baby train to slow downShe did not sound worried. If anything, she sounded a little surprised at how easy it has been. “Sometimes I forget I have a bump on my life. I feel really blessed. I don’t have crazy pregnancies for the most part,” she tells PEOPLE.That does not mean she is going full speed. The Grammy winner said she still has to ease off as the day wears on. “So this mom is rolling. Now don’t get me wrong, at a certain point in the day, I got to slow it down,” Ciara tells PEOPLE. “I’m feeling all kinds of stuff happening, but all in all, I feel really good. I feel really blessed. I’m excited for the new little one.”She added that she cannot wait to meet the baby. She is “really happy and thankful” heading into the holiday season.Wilson, a retired NFL player and now an analyst for CBS Sports, was in a good mood too. “We always have a good time this time of year,” he says, before pointing out a pattern in the family calendar. “It’s been like every three years,” he tells PEOPLE, as Ciara responds, “Oh, stop it. I think it’s time for the train to slow down.”They have not shared the baby’s gender. The couple married in 2016 and already have three children together: Sienna Princess, 9, Win Harrison, 6, and Amora Princess, 2. Ciara is also mom to Future Zahir, 12, whom she shares with her ex-fiancé Future, whose real name is Nayvadius DeMun Cash.The kids are ready and the holidays are closeAt home, the big siblings seem to be fully on board. Ciara says the kids “are so sweet with the new little one” and keep showering her with belly kisses. “They always kiss my belly. They’re really clear on what’s happening. I think we need to say the baby is the gift,” she adds.Santaland at Macy’s Herald Square opens Nov. 27. Visitors can ride a train called the North Star Express, grab hot cocoa and stop for photos on the way to Santa.“It’s an honor to be here. We all know how iconic Macy’s is ... And I’ve, over the years, been so fortunate to participate in the Macy’s Day Parade. So many great memories here. Our kids brand, 3Brand, is actually in the Macy’s store,” she tells PEOPLE.Macy’s picked the family to host the moment. “It’s pretty cool,” she adds. The baby train may be slowing down, but the North Star Express is about to start running.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: One of the greatest comebacks: How former Kansas City Chiefs' star Eric Berry went from battling cancer to earning the NFL’s highest honors
articles.summary: Eric Berry, the former Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, might have had a lot of talent and skills but things went haywire in his life when he was
articles.body: Eric Berry, the former Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, might have had a lot of talent and skills but things went haywire in his life when he was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma in December 2014 after a mass was discovered in his chest. At the peak of his career, Eric Berry had to leave his career but that was not the end of his story.Eric Berry fought against cancer and came back to the field to achieve a record breaking performance for the Kansas City ChiefsEric Berry took some time off as the Kansas City Chiefs stood by his side after his diagnosis in December 2014.In the next few months, Eric Berry remained aggressive with his treatment and in 2015, he bounced back on the field after he was declared cancer free by doctors.Despite fighting against cancer, Eric Berry recorded a pretty impressive performance in 2015 when he returned to the field.Eric Berry appeared in all 16 games (15 starts), recording 61 combined tackles (55 solo), 10 passes defended, and 2 interceptions for 40 return yards. He helped the Kansas City Chiefs win 10 straight regular season games to reach the playoffs.In the Wild Card round, Eric Berry recorded 3 tackles and a first-quarter interception in a 30–0 shutout win over the Houston Texans.This also led Eric Berry to win Comeback Player of the Year with 38 of 50 votes as well as a Pro Bowl selection and First-Team All-Pro honors.In an interview with reporters back then, Eric Berry had reflected on his achievements as he said, "To be honest with you, I think it will mean a lot for the people who followed my story—the people who are going through things and fighting through something like cancer…”He added, “I just wanted to show those people anything is possible and that you can't let anything come between you and your dreams. "As long as somebody sees my story and is inspired, I think that was my main goal going through everything that I went through—just being strong for people who couldn't be strong for themselves."The Kansas City Chiefs Chairman and CEO Clark Hunt also opened up on Eric Berry’s comeback as he said, "Eric is a very, very special person. And I say that even not taking into consideration the health problems he's had over the past year—overcoming cancer. He's somebody who has been a great player and a team leader. His ability and willingness to come back from the cancer treatments that he'd been through in early 2015 says so much about him as a person.”The billionaire owner added, "I think that desire and that passion for the game really had an impact on the Chiefs throughout the 2016 season. I think he was somebody they could rally around early in the year when things weren't going well. He wasn't somebody who put his head down and he really helped the team get the season turned around and make the playoffs."Eric Berry’s injury in 2017 changed his career for himIn the 2016 season, Eric Berry started all 16 games, recording 77 combined tackles, 4 interceptions, and 2 defensive touchdowns.However, in 2017, he tore his Achilles tendon which marked a turning point in his career as it ended the season for him after just one game.A year later, a painful Haglund's deformity on his heel sidelined him for nearly the entire 2018 season and he was later released by the Kansas City Chiefs in 2019.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: They were NFL losers last year. Now they’re playoff contenders.
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns, Cincinatti Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs, New York Giants, Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings all missed the 2025 playoffs, but now make up nearly half of this season’s projected postseason field.
articles.body: If you haven’t been paying much attention to the NFL, this season’s projected playoff field might look unrecognizable. Cleveland? Cincinnati? Kansas City? The New York Giants? One year ago, each endured a brutal 2025 season that left them with six or fewer wins and watching the playoffs from home. Fast-forward to this fall, when after 10 weeks, they’ve already won more games than they did all of last year. Those turnarounds have put them in the driver’s seat for the upcoming playoffs — and they’re not alone in going from missing out to becoming a postseason factor. Both Detroit and Minnesota missed the NFC’s final playoff spot last season while finishing 9-8 in a brutally difficult NFC North. Now, both are 7-2. The NFL’s postseason includes 14 teams; if the current playoff projections were to hold, the Browns, Bengals, Chiefs, Giants, Lions and Vikings would make up nearly half the field only 12 months after failing to make the last postseason. Their revival is a reminder of how quickly franchises’ fortunes can change. Their quick turnarounds don’t owe to a few shared traits. Each ranks in the league’s upper half in fewest points allowed. Most draw around the league average in penalties and create around the league average in turnovers. The biggest catalyst for the Giants’ (5-3-1) switch from the bottom of the NFC East to its top took place when they hired longtime coach John Harbaugh in the offseason. Yet all of their months of planning for a new era were upended in only Week 2, when starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. New York patched together the position before taking a leap of faith and trading for J.J. McCarthy, a 2024 first-round pick who had quickly lost the Vikings’ confidence. In New York, McCarthy hasn’t turned into an overnight passing sensation in his four games as starter, with only two touchdowns and two interceptions. Still, his rating and completion percentage are better than the Giants’ previous backup, which in the middling NFC East has kept the Giants in first place. By leading the NFL in blitzes and pressure — including eight sacks in Sunday’s key win against NFC North rival Green Bay — Minnesota’s defense has kept the team competitive all season and has provided a high floor for their potential. Their playoff ceiling will be determined by their offense, however. “All we have to do is be mediocre at this point,” star receiver Justin Jefferson said Sunday. Getting to mediocre has taken the entire season. After Minnesota soured on McCarthy last winter, it added veteran quarterback Kyler Murray. When Murray was less than inspiring, too, it played backup Carson Wentz. When he couldn’t bring life to one of the NFL’s least explosive offenses, either, the Vikings traded for Las Vegas starter Kirk Cousins at last week’s trade deadline, in a move that instantly paid off. How anemic was Minnesota’s offense? Even after scoring 30 points against the Packers, the Vikings have still scored only 15 touchdowns this season, second-worst in the NFL. In Detroit, the opposite story has unfolded: The Lions’ defense looked to be a liability during the season’s first month while quarterback Jared Goff, receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and back Jahmyr Gibbs helped the Lions score 30 or more points in four of their first five games. Since allowing 29.6 points per game over the season’s first five games, the Lions have rebounded to allow just 12.7 in their last four — all wins. Detroit’s challenge is sustaining that defensive improvement. Since Nov. 1, the unit has suffered a pair of devastating injuries. Starting linebacker Jack Campbell was hospitalized Nov. 1 due to a neck injury, while star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson tore a knee ligament while celebrating a sack in Week 10 and will miss the season. “We will pick up the slack and it’s going to require a lot of guys doing — it’s going to require a lot out of everybody,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said. “One guy cannot pick up the slack of (Hutchinson), but we have enough here to weather this storm and rise above it.” Kansas City was perhaps the most predictable turnaround. The Chiefs were unusually poor in one-score games in 2025, then lost superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes to a knee injury. Neither seemed likely to repeat in 2026. Yet the Chiefs have done more than simply stabilize themselves this fall — at times, they’ve looked as strong as the vintage Chiefs teams that turned the team into a dynasty. Mahomes’ averages this season for yards gained per pass attempt and yards gained per catch are both above his career averages. The combination of Mahomes and offseason acquisition running back Kenneth Walker III has improved the Chiefs this season in virtually every offensive category, notably jumping from 25th in rushing offense to fifth this season. In Cleveland, it’s not unusual for the Browns to already be out of contention this deep into the season; the franchise has played in just four playoff games since 1995 and won just once. They’re still in the hunt despite being outscored 78-13 in first quarters. All six of their wins have come by four points or fewer. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has become a comeback artist, with four of the wins requiring a double-digit comeback, including Sunday’s win over Houston that saw the Browns erase a 17-0 hole. “I wish collectively him and I together would play better early and coach better early so that we didn’t have to get to this,” Browns coach Todd Monken said Sunday. “It’s been a credit to our team, our guys up front. We have a special group, and it says a lot about Deshaun.” One of the hottest teams in the league is Cincinnati, which has scored 30 or more points in a franchise-record five consecutive games. Quarterback Joe Burrow’s 310 passing yards per game and his 27 passing touchdowns lead the NFL. “Impossible to say anyone is playing better than him,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said.

articles.title: “Obviously playing worse”: Mina Kimes questions Josh Allen’s progress as Bills star faces unexpected criticism despite MVP-level numbers
articles.summary: ESPN analyst Mina Kimes says Josh Allen is playing worse this season than last, even though the Buffalo Bills sit at 8-1.
articles.body: ESPN analyst Mina Kimes says Josh Allen is playing worse this season than last, even though the Buffalo Bills sit at 8-1. Kimes made the case on Tuesday’s The Mina Kimes Show while discussing MVP candidates through Week 10 with Ben Solak. She left Allen out of the conversation. The numbers tell a different story. Allen is on pace to match or beat his 2025 production in most areas, and on Sunday he broke an NFL record in a 31-12 win over the New York Jets. The Bills have also done it while missing key receivers.Mina Kimes questions Josh Allen’s progress despite his numbersKimes did not hedge. Asked about the top MVP candidates, she moved past Allen quickly.“Josh Allen, we haven’t spent much time talking about,” Kimes said on The Mina Kimes Show on Tuesday. “Like I said, I think he’s asked to do a lot, but he’s obviously playing worse than he did last year, to my eyes, so I just don’t see it personally.”The phrase “to my eyes” matters, because the box score does not back her up the way she suggests. Allen won MVP in 2024, and Buffalo is 8-1 even with his best wide receivers hurt and James Cook fumbling.Allen’s completion rate has slipped, from 69.3 percent last year to 65.0 percent through nine games. That is the strongest part of her argument. Almost everything else points the other way.Allen’s touchdown pace and the new NFL recordAt his current pace, Allen would throw for more yards than in 2025 and match last year’s 25 passing touchdowns. He is also on pace for 13 interceptions, three more than last season. That cost is real. Ball security elsewhere has improved, though: no fumbles in nine games, after six last year, two of them lost.The rushing numbers are where he pulls away. Allen ran for 14 touchdowns in 2025 and is on pace for 21 this year, with about the same yardage.“Josh Allen is on pace for 25 pass TDs and 21 rush TDs,” NFL analyst Michael F. Florio wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. “There’s never been a 20-20 season.”Sunday added to the case. Allen’s 1-yard rushing score in the first half of the 31-12 win over the Jets was his 323rd career touchdown.“Josh Allen rushes for the touchdown, marking his 323rd career total touchdown,” Buffalo Bills PR wrote on its official X account on Sunday. “Allen, nine games into his ninth season, has surpassed Peyton Manning (322) for the most total TDs all-time by a player in their first 10 seasons.”He later added another rushing touchdown and a passing touchdown, lifting his career total to 325. His 24 total touchdowns this season are more than 15 NFL teams have.Kimes can have her read. A quarterback who is slipping rarely rewrites the record book on a Sunday afternoon.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: B/R's Week 11 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: The stretch run to the fantasy playoffs is here.
articles.body:
The stretch run to the fantasy playoffs is here.

The last month of the fantasy regular season means different things for different managers. The fortunate few sitting at 8-2 or better are just trying to keep rolling and secure a first-round bye. The cellar-dwellers are playing out the string and hoping to play spoiler—misery loves company.

But for a large group of fantasy managers sitting anywhere from 6-4 to 4-6, nothing has been decided. Put together a winning streak, and it's on to the postseason. Hit the skids over the final month, and when that regular season ends, so will fantasy football for 2026.

We're here to help you start the stretch run with a victory, offering position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to the sortable player rankings for Week 11, a few notes.

The first is the same as always: The overall rankings feature the top 124 players to help fantasy managers make flex lineup decisions, but they do not include quarterbacks. The list of viable fantasy options under center isn't getting any longer, but if your league features a superflex spot and you have a decent QB2, he should go in said spot.

The second note is a depressing one—it's the Byepocalypse. Six teams are off in Week 11—the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks. No Bijan Robinson this week. No Jaxon Smith-Njigba this week. No Harold Fannin Jr. this week. No Jordan Love or Christian Watson this week.

Finally, if you're sitting at 5-5 or worse, don't be afraid to get aggressive with lineup decisions. We have reached the point in the season where many fantasy managers simply cannot afford another loss. So, if there's a matchup play you like, start them.

The only person who has to live with your lineup decisions is you. And if you're going to go down, it might as well be swinging.

Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals has been channeling his inner Godzilla over the last month, flattening opposing defenses.

After throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns against the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, the 29-year-old has 20 touchdown passes over his last five games. It marked his fourth game with at least four touchdown passes and his third with more than 400 passing yards during that stretch.

After nine games, Burrow leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7) and touchdown passes (27). He's leading the AFC in passing yards and passed Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills for the top spot among QBs in fantasy points last week.

Having a loaded offense certainly doesn't hurt, but Burrow is playing like the NFL's MVP right now.

After a slow start to the season, Drake Maye of the New England Patriots entered Week 9 fourth in fantasy points among quarterbacks. But last Sunday's trip to Germany was a disaster—he fractured his ankle on the first drive of the game and is expected to be out for the season.

Maye wasn't the only quarterback who got banged up last week. Geno Smith of the New York Jets took a beating against the Buffalo Bills, suffering an ankle injury of his own in the process.

There's a chance Smith will be able to play Sunday against the Chargers, but if he can't go, rookie Cade Klubnik would draw his first NFL start.

If Smith sits, Klubnik would join several inexperienced quarterbacks starting in Week 11, further limiting reliable fantasy options.

We are heading into a week when Fernando Mendoza (Las Vegas Raiders), Joe Milton III (Philadelphia Eagles), Carson Beck (Arizona Cardinals) and Kyle McCord (Miami Dolphins) will all be starting. That sound you hear is fantasy managers sobbing quietly.

Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

Mahomes broke out of his mid-season funk in a big way last week, throwing for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Atlanta Falcons. That performance got him back into the top 10 for the season, and this week he faces a Cardinals team allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks.

Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

After roasting the Dallas Cowboys to the tune of 389 yards and three scores last week, Purdy sits third in fantasy points among quarterbacks. But this week he goes from facing one of the league's worst defenses to one of the best—the Minnesota Vikings just shut down Jordan Love and the Packers at Lambeau Field.

Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans (at Dallas Cowboys)

Ward has upped his play over his last two games—the second-year pro has thrown four touchdown passes and ranks seventh in fantasy points per game among quarterbacks over that span. Now he takes on a Cowboys defense that just allowed the most yards at home in franchise history.

Kenneth Walker III has been outstanding in his first season with the Chiefs, but after injuring his groin in practice last week, he missed Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons.

You wouldn't have known it by the team's offensive performance.

In his most extensive game action of the season, rookie Emmett Johnson rolled in Atlanta—the fifth-rounder from Nebraska carried the ball 22 times for 101 yards and added six receptions for 70 yards and a pair of touchdowns on the way to 35.1 PPR points—tops among all AFC running backs.

If Walker remains sidelined, Johnson would again have a significant role against the Cardinals.

Walker wasn't the only running back who got banged up in Week 10. Woody Marks of the Houston Texans is in the concussion protocol and unlikely to play Thursday night. TreVeyon Henderson of the New England Patriots will be out indefinitely after landing on injured reserve with an illness.

If Walker's success this season was surprising, then Chuba Hubbard's is an absolute stunner. After racking up 172 total yards and two touchdowns last week against the New Orleans Saints, the Carolina Panthers back is eighth in the league in rushing and is one of four backs averaging over 20 PPR points per game.

Thanks to a pair of short-yardage scores and five receptions, Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens managed a top-12 fantasy finish in Week 10. But he had just 20 total yards in the game. He hasn't run for 100 yards since Week 5 and barely ranks among the top 25 running backs in fantasy points since that outing.

Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans (at Dallas Cowboys)

Pollard's streak of 100-yard games on the ground came to an end last week against the Jaguars, but he still managed 99 total yards and a touchdown. Pollard is averaging 4.4 yards per carry and a career-high 69.8 rushing yards per game, and this week he takes on a Dallas defense that was just savaged by Christian McCaffrey for 223 total yards and three scores.

Bucky Irving, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (at Detroit Lions)

Over the past several weeks, Irving essentially has been the offense for the Buccaneers—he's seventh in the league in carries and fifth in rushing yards. But this week's matchup with the Lions is a bad one for fantasy managers—Detroit is fifth in run defense and has surrendered the third-fewest PPR points per game to running backs in 2026.

David Montgomery, Houston Texans (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

Montgomery hasn't played in over a month, hasn't had more than 60 rushing yards in a game and is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. But with Marks in the concussion protocol, Montgomery should see as many touches as he can handle against a Colts team allowing the seventh-most PPR points per game to running backs.

We finally figured out how to slow Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba: a bye week.

Smith-Njigba is on pace to become the NFL's first 2,000-yard wideout and leads all receivers in PPR points by a wide margin, but over the past month at least it's Ja'Marr Chase of the Cincinnati Bengals who leads the position in PPR points per game.

Last week against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Chase blew up to the tune of 11 catches for 231 yards. It was the third straight game in which he has had over 100 receiving yards and double-digit catches, and the second game in a row where he had 100 receiving yards before halftime.

Chase is the AFC's highest-scoring wide receiver after 10 weeks, but he's not the one-man band that Smith-Njigba is in Seattle. Chase's teammate, Tee Higgins, is averaging over 19 PPR points per game and is a top-10 fantasy option in his own right.

Chase and Higgins may be the best of the AFC's dynamic duos at wide receiver, but they aren't the only pair of pass-catchers doing damage for fantasy managers. Christian Watson (WR4) and Matthew Golden (WR6) of the Green Bay Packers and CeeDee Lamb (WR2) and George Pickens (WR9) of the Dallas Cowboys have also been highly productive.

It has been a miserable season of injuries at the wide receiver position, and the hits kept coming in Week 10. A.J. Brown returned for New England but suffered a hamstring injury in the same game that saw Drake Maye injured. New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. also went down with an ankle issue.

Deebo Samuel of the San Francisco 49ers is one of the wide receivers who have missed significant time this year, but last week in Dallas Samuel was back on the field in a performance that harkened back to his heyday with the Niners—Samuel amassed 109 total yards and scored a pair of touchdowns against the Cowboys.

DK Metcalf, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Philadelphia Eagles)

It has been a disappointing season for Metcalf, extending his struggles in Pittsburgh. This week offers a prime opportunity to rebound against an Eagles team allowing the most PPR points per game in the NFC to wide receivers. Another quiet outing would make it harder for fantasy managers to trust him down the stretch.

D.J. Moore, Buffalo Bills (vs. Miami Dolphins)

Moore is coming off four catches for 90 yards and a touchdown in last week's win over the New York Jets, but backing that performance up in Week 11 won't be easy. Miami is a bad team, but it has been stingy to opposing wide receivers, allowing the third-fewest PPR points per game to the position.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (vs. Tennessee Titans)

Calling Flournoy a "sleeper" may be pushing it—after six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown against the 49ers last week, Flournoy is a top-25 fantasy receiver for the season. His career year should continue this week against the Titans—no team has given up more PPR points to wideouts this year.

After missing the first two games of the 2026 season due to knee surgery, Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders didn't waste any time getting back up to speed—entering last week's tilt with the Seattle Seahawks, he led all tight ends in fantasy points per game.

But Bowers went down early in the loss to Seattle with an ankle injury, and while it isn't believed to be season-ending, head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that Bowers' status is up in the air for Week 11's trip to Denver.

"We're still evaluating him," Kubiak said. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury."

Beyond his ankle injury, Bowers' fantasy outlook faces another concern heading into the stretch run—the Raiders managed just 98 passing yards with Fernando Mendoza under center in Week 10.

Bowers isn't the only high-end fantasy tight end with quarterback problems. With rookie Carson Beck under center, Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals caught five passes for 37 yards. There are some tight ends for whom that would be an OK week, but it was McBride's first game of the year under 10 PPR points.

Bowers also isn't the only tight end with injury issues, which is rather a drag given the lack of depth at the position. Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs tweaked his ankle against the Falcons but is expected to play in Week 11, while T.J. Hockenson missed Minnesota's win over the Green Bay Packers with a wrist injury.

Fantasy managers who rolled the dice on a breakout season from New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely have been rewarded—especially of late. After catching nine passes for 127 yards and a touchdown in last week's loss to the Washington Commanders, Likely is the only tight end in fantasy averaging 20 PPR points since Week 5.

Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills (vs. Miami Dolphins)

Josh Allen isn't a quarterback who will force the action—he hits whoever is open in a given week. In Week 11 that should mean no shortage of targets for Kincaid. As stingy as the Dolphins have been to opposing wide receivers, they have been equally generous to tight ends.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Philadelphia Eagles)

The Steelers imploded offensively last week, in no small part because Freiermuth and Darnell Washington were non-factors despite a plus fantasy matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Things aren't likely to improve significantly this week—the Eagles have surrendered the fourth-fewest PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

Mike Gesicki, Cincinnati Bengals (at Washington Commanders)

Gesicki ranks outside the top 15 at tight end for the season, and he's heavily reliant on touchdowns for fantasy production. But he should snap out of his recent funk Monday night in the nation's capital—only the Lions have allowed more PPR points per game to tight ends this season.

For most of this season, the Minnesota Vikings have been the top fantasy defense, and the 21st-century Purple People Eaters just feasted on the Packers at Green Bay to the tune of eight sacks and four takeaways.

But this week may be the team's biggest test yet.

To be clear, the Vikings are an every-week start. They are second in the league in total defense and pass defense, lead the league in scoring defense and sacks, rank third in the NFL in takeaways and retook the top spot in fantasy points last week.

But this week in Mexico City, Minnesota faces a difficult matchup with the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers.

The 49ers are pacing the NFL in total offense, rank seventh in passing, third in rushing and second in points per game—despite a number of injuries on offense. No quarterback has been sacked fewer times than Brock Purdy, and San Francisco is 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to defenses.

Another big outing isn't going to be easy.

After a slow start, the Detroit Lions have improved defensively, ranking sixth among fantasy defenses over the last month. However, the injury suffered by star edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson last week raises concerns about their ability to sustain that improvement.

The Houston Texans were the first defense drafted in more than a few fantasy leagues over the summer, but after last week's loss in Cleveland, they are now a matchup-dependent option. Houston ranks outside the top 15 in fantasy points among defenses and has posted just two top-five weekly finishes all season.

At this point in the season, there have been eight kickers who have made at least 20 field goals. Of that group, two—Tyler Bass of the Buffalo Bills and Chase McLaughlin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers—have yet to miss a field goal. Bass has, however, whiffed on a pair of extra points. No one's perfect.

Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

The Chiefs might not have a star-studded defense, but they are eighth in the NFL in yards allowed, third in points allowed and among the top five in fantasy scoring at the position since their bye. With rookie quarterback Carson Beck coming to Arrowhead this week, Kansas City looks like a strong fantasy option.

Ka'imi Fairbairn, Houston Texans (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

Fairbairn has missed just one field-goal attempt this season, and on Thursday night the Texans host a Colts team allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to kickers.

The Buccaneers have been solid for fantasy managers this season—Tampa ranks fourth in fantasy points for the season and first (by a wide margin) in points per game over the last month. But traveling to Detroit to face the Lions is about as bad as matchups get for defenses.

Chase McLaughlin, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (at Detroit Lions)

Fantasy managers who have McLaughlin rostered are rightfully reluctant to move on. But the Lions are a rotten fantasy matchup for kickers, and the Buccaneers could struggle to generate offense this week.

The Bills have played better defensively over the past few weeks, although a series of favorable matchups played a role in that. The Bills get another one Sunday against a Miami Dolphins team allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to defenses this year.

Ryan Fitzgerald, Carolina Panthers (vs. Baltimore Ravens)

It has been an up-and-down season for Fitzgerald, who has already missed on five point-after tries. But the Ravens should give him a chance to get it going—Baltimore has allowed the third-most fantasy points to kickers this season.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.body:
It's almost Thanksgiving, which means that winter is right around the corner. As the temperatures drop and rain turns to snow, weather is likely to be an increasingly large factor on the NFL landscape.

Fortunately, we haven't reached the point of subzero air and frozen fields just yet. However, we could still see weather play a role in Week 11, which will open with Thursday night's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans.

Here, we'll take an early look at the full Week 11 schedule, the latest odds, and the most accurate forecast information from The Weather Channel to make a few predictions.

Indianapolis Colts (+11.5) at Houston Texans (Retractable Roof)

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 10MPH, Low of 49°F

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Winds up to 20MPH, High of 64°F

Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Winds up to 10MPH, High of 65°F

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 20MPH, High of 53°F
