Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 65°F

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions (Dome)

Arizona Cardinals (+15.5) at Kansas City Chiefs

Forecast: Mostly Sunny, Winds up to 10MPH, High of 52°F

Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles

Forecast: Rain, Winds up to 10MPH, High of 64°F

New York Jets (+3.5) at Los Angeles Chargers (Dome)

Jacksonville Jaguars (-5.5) at New York Giants

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 50°F

Las Vegas Raiders (+9.5) at Denver Broncos

Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers (in Mexico City)

Cincinnati Bengals (-5.5) at Washington Commanders

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 10MPH, Low of 37°F

Bye Week: Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, Seattle Seahawks

Week 11 will bring a bit of a condensed schedule, as a whopping six teams will be on bye. Based on the early lines, the week is likely to bring a lot of lopsided games, too.

It will begin with the Texans and Colts on Thursday. The Texans blew another winnable game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, but Indy has essentially given up on its season by trading away several key contributors. Still hoping to steal a playoff spot, Houston should look to make a statement on Thursday night.

The Baltimore Ravens are also desperate to stay alive, as are the Carolina Panthers. Their battle should be one of the more entertaining games of the early afternoon schedule. Don't sleep on the Tennessee Titans and Dallas Cowboys matchup, either, as it could be more competitive than many expect.

Tennessee's offense has started to show signs of life recently, and Dallas' defense remains an embarrassment.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Detroit Lions matchup would be more fun if both teams were healthy. However, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield is questionable with an ankle injury, while the Lions have lost star pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL.

The Pennsylvania showdown between the Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers could be quite fun, especially with rain in the forecast. The Steelers have the more complete team and the healthier roster. However, we could see a track meet on the ground, as Saquon Barkley and Jaylen Warren trade blows on a soggy field.

The Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants matchup is probably the best game in the late-afternoon window, and Sunday's nightcap should be fantastic.

The Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers will face off at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City. It's a game that could determine the team to beat in the NFC.

The 49ers have looked like the conference's top team for most of the season, but the Vikings have boasted the league's best defense. With the arrival of quarterback Kirk Cousins, Minnesota looks like a legitimate title contender.

Monday's game could be a bit anticlimactic, as the Washington Commanders aren't really equipped to keep pace with the Cincinnati Bengals. Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on fire, and home-field advantage probably won't be enough to even the playing field.

articles.title: Every NFL Team's Midseason MVP
articles.summary: Now that every NFL team has at least nine games under its belt, the second half of the 2026 season is officially underway.
articles.body:
Now that every NFL team has at least nine games under its belt, the second half of the 2026 season is officially underway.

Who stands out the most as we prepare for the stretch run? Let's break down every team's most valuable player so far.

And because it's a quarterback-driven league, we'll also spotlight a non-QB MVP for every team where a signal-caller takes the top honor.

He's the centerpiece of the league's top-scoring offense and the No. 1 seed in the AFC. The guy is tied for the league lead in rushing touchdowns and is a prime candidate for league MVP.

Non-QB MVP: Edge Greg Rousseau —A case could be made for AFC rushing yardage leader James Cook, but Rousseau is the only player in the NFL with at least eight sacks and three forced fumbles.

There's just no way it can go to anyone on offense considering that unit's struggles. Rodriguez has 80 tackles, a sack, a pick, and a forced fumble, putting him in contention for Defensive Rookie of the Year. He edges out Jordyn Brooks and Chop Robinson.

Maye had a 116.2 passer rating in his last six games before suffering a devastating ankle injury in Week 10. He was undoubtedly carrying them.

Non-QB MVP: LB Christian Elliss —The heart and soul of the defense had a team-high 75 tackles along with five tackles for loss. He's on track to make his first Pro Bowl.

A prime Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate, Bailey has 7.5 sacks and is tied for the league lead with five forced fumbles. He's already become the key cog in this defense.

The do-everything 25-year-old is performing at a first-team All-Pro level for a team that has been crushed by injuries at quarterback.

With a ridiculous 27 touchdown passes and a 117.7 rating, the 29-year-old has built a strong case for league MVP while commanding an offense that has scored more than 30 points in five consecutive wins.

Non-QB MVP: (Tie) WRs Ja'Marr Chase & Tee Higgins —You can't choose. Higgins has actually been more productive on a per-reception and per-target basis, but Chase leads the team in catches, yards and touchdowns. Both are playing out of their minds.

I'd also accept Denzel Ward or Quincy Williams the way they've performed for a defense that has been surprisingly solid early in the post-Myles Garrett era. Schwesinger is one of just three players in the league with more than 100 tackles, and he's also recorded three sacks and three forced fumbles.

The Steelers are in contention primarily because of their seventh-ranked scoring defense, and Watt leads the way with 7.5 sacks, a pick-six and the league's highest Pro Football Focus run defense grade among edge defenders.

Where did this come from? Stroud has thrown 19 touchdown passes to just three interceptions and the Texans have a top-10 scoring offense. He's back! Now he just needs some support from the supposedly world-class defense.

Non-QB MVP: Edge Will Anderson Jr. —The Defensive Player of the Year favorite leads the NFL with 10.5 sacks.

The three-time Pro Bowler is on the verge of 1,000 scrimmage yards and has scored eight touchdowns despite being surrounded by dwindling talent on a bad team.

Jacksonville Jaguars: QB Trevor Lawrence

He's got a 112.8 passer rating and the Jaguars are the league's fourth-highest-scoring team. You couldn't ask for much more.

Non-QB MVP: CB Travis Hunter —Quarterbacks have a mere 60.0 passer rating when targeting Hunter, who has three interceptions in a breakout sophomore campaign.

This is tricky with Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker off the roster, but the 30-year-old has put up 7.5 sacks and 17 quarterback hits. He beats out running back Tony Pollard, who is on pace to go over 1,000 yards with double-digit touchdowns.

Making the Case for NFL MVP Favorites And Darkhorses 🏆

Nik Bonitto is right there as well, but Allen is more of a consistent playmaking force. Only Rousseau (27) has more quarterback hits than he does (23).

It's been a big bounce-back year for the legend, who has 19 touchdown throws to four picks as the league's fourth-highest-rated passer for a top-10 scoring offense.

Non-QB MVP: Edge George Karlaftis —Kenneth Walker III has 11 touchdowns in eight games and Chris Jones is balling out again, but Karlaftis has 5.5 sacks, 21 quarterback hits, an interception and a forced fumble. He's the primary reason this is the league's third-ranked scoring defense.

Maxx Crosby is having another great season but the defense has still been awful. The Raiders are averaging a strong 25.1 points per game, thanks primarily to the work of their superstar tight end. Bowers leads all NFL players at that position with 676 receiving yards.

Los Angeles Chargers: Edge Tuli Tuipulotu

Can it be nobody? At least the team's best defensive player has 16 quarterback hits and has shined as a versatile weapon. The defense has been decent after a terrible start to the campaign.

Lamb ranks second only to Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 976 receiving yards and has caught eight touchdown passes as the primary weapon in an offense that ranks fifth in scoring. That's enough to beat out Quinnen Williams, who is having a tremendous season but hasn't been able to turn around a struggling defense.

You could just as easily bestow this on Abdul Carter or rookie Arvell Reese, but Holland was one of the most dominant defensive players in the league during the Giants' strong start. He's the only player in the league with four interceptions and multiple forced fumbles.

With 65 tackles, Baun leads the team by a huge margin and has consistently been a do-everything force in the middle of all the action for a squad that has otherwise fallen apart.

Washington Commanders: QB Jayden Daniels

He's still not where he was as a rookie, but Daniels hadn't thrown an interception all season until Week 10. He has the lowest qualified pick rate in the league while guiding a mediocre team that lacks standout players elsewhere.

Non-QB MVP: G Sam Cosmi —I can't imagine where this team would be if not for Cosmi, who has been one of the best pass-blocking guards in the league this year. PFF grades him third among qualifiers.

The man quarterbacking the league's seventh-highest-scoring offense has generally been brilliant when healthy.

Non-QB MVP: LB Devin Bush —This could eventually be Jeffery Simmons, but he hasn't logged enough time there yet. For now, Bush gets credit for emerging as the linchpin of a defense loaded with killer instinct.

Nobody's debating us on this one. As well as Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown have performed, the Offensive Player of the Year frontrunner easily takes this award with a league-best 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine games.

Williams and Xavier McKinney lead the way. McKinney has a league-best six interceptions, but Williams has dominated across the board as PFF's highest-graded safety. Both have a shot at earning first-team All-Pro honors, having saved this defense in the absence of the injured Micah Parsons.

He and Arvell Reese are the only players in the league with more than 75 tackles and at least four sacks, but Cashman has done it in only eight games. He's also tied for the team lead with seven passes defended. The 30-year-old is the focal point of the league's No. 1 defense.

The Falcons have won three games this season. In two of those victories, Robinson was an absolute monster, totaling 339 yards from scrimmage and four touchdowns as Atlanta combined to score 80 points. Overall, he's already over 1,200 yards from scrimmage through 10 games. This is a no-doubter.

Lloyd, the team's tackle leader with 63, has two sacks and three interceptions (including a pick-six). Derrick Brown, Jaelan Phillips and rookie Zakee Wheatley have all made big impacts on D, but nobody has made game-changing plays like Lloyd.

You could give this to Young, Carl Granderson or Kaden Elliss. Young trails Granderson in sacks, eight to 8.5, but leads him in quarterback hits, 15 to 10, and has also forced a fumble. Meanwhile, Elliss has missed a third of the season to date.

Irving has three 100-yard performances on the ground this season, and those are Tampa Bay's only wins to date. With 584 rushing yards and seven total touchdowns in his last five games, he's one of the hottest backs in football.

McBride ranks second in the NFL with 78 receptions. He's the first player in NFL history to catch at least seven passes in each of his team's first nine games of a season. The guy has little support but is balling.

I don't care that he's missed a few games—McDuffie is an absolute wall. Opposing quarterbacks have a 22.9 passer rating and are averaging just 2.9 yards per target when throwing at the 26-year-old this season.

Purdy has the league's top QBR at 81.4, thanks in part to a wild 9.0 yards-per-attempt average. He's a prime MVP candidate in his fifth season.

Non-QB MVP: LB Fred Warner —You could almost make a case for him over Purdy. Five forced fumbles and 88 tackles! The four-time first-team All-Pro is playing the best football of his career, leaving no room for Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle or Trent Williams in this conversation.

Smith-Njigba is already over 1,200 receiving yards, while nobody else in football has reached 1,000. He's head and shoulders above every other player at his position and is likely to battle Gibbs for Offensive Player of the Year honors.

articles.title: Week 11 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Review for Fantasy Football's Top Fringe Starters
articles.summary: Many fantasy football managers will be forced to rely on fringe starters in Week 11. In addition to a growing list of key injuries, managers will have to deal with having six teams on bye.
articles.body:
Many fantasy football managers will be forced to rely on fringe starters in Week 11. In addition to a growing list of key injuries, managers will have to deal with having six teams on bye.

The Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks will have the week off. This means that even healthy rosters are unlikely to have all of their stars available.

Here, you'll find some early start/sit recommendations for popular second-tier options based on recent performances, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai has been sidelined with thumb and toe injuries. However, he returned to practice this week and has said that he's "on track" to return on Sunday, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin .

Monangai's status will bear watching, of course, but if he is healthy, he'll be worth putting back in the lineup.

Chicago's No. 2 back behind D'Andre Swift has played a fairly prominent offensive role when healthy, dating back to last season. He has only appeared in four games this season but has topped 20 fantasy points twice.

Monangai should reach double-digit fantasy points this week in a complementary role. The Bears are set to host the New Orleans Saints, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Sit: Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally started to lean into the two-headed rushing attack of Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks. After being an afterthought through the first few weeks of 2026, Gainwell has gone three straight games with at least eight fantasy points and has reached double digits in each of his last two.

The issue this week is that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with foot and ankle injuries that leave his status for Week 11 uncertain.

Backup Jalon Daniels has proven to be a capable fill-in, but Mayfield being out of the lineup limits Gainwell's ceiling as a pass-catcher. That's a problem because his floor as a runner will be limited this week.

Gainwell is clearly the No. 2 ball-carrier behind Irving, and he's about to face a Detroit Lions defense that has surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs in 2026.

Start: Elic Ayomanor, WR, Tennessee Titans

Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh recently admitted that the team has opened things up a bit for quarterback Cam Ward and the offense in recent weeks.

"The change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not is he capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that," Saleh told reporters .

The shift in offensive philosophy has helped the stock of wide receiver Elic Ayomanor, who has topped six fantasy points in each of the last three weeks. Ayomanor is coming off a 12.9-point outing and could easily replicate it against the Dallas Cowboys this week.

Dallas has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season. Given the Cowboys' ability to put points on the board, Ward should do plenty of passing, giving Ayomanor a very alluring fantasy floor.

Buffalo Bills receiver Keon Coleman has rewarded fantasy managers with a few solid games this season. However, they have usually come when new No. 1 receiver D.J. Moore was either sidelined or at less than 100 percent.

Moore was in the lineup and healthy last week against the New York Jets. He led Buffalo with four catches and 90 yards, while Coleman was limited to just one 11-yard reception.

It's impossible to trust Coleman this week in a matchup with the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo should look to lean on the run against Miami, which has surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

Coleman hasn't produced double-digit fantasy points since Week 6, and he's likely to underwhelm again in Week 11.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Best Football Movies of All Time
articles.summary: What makes a football movie great is in the eye of the beholder. But pretty much everyone is looking for some combination of a) an inspiring story, b) realistic on-field action, c) a lasting impact on sports fans and d) quotable and/or rewatchable scenes that become iconic over time.
articles.body:
What makes a football movie great is in the eye of the beholder. But pretty much everyone is looking for some combination of a) an inspiring story, b) realistic on-field action, c) a lasting impact on sports fans and d) quotable and/or rewatchable scenes that become iconic over time.

With that in mind, we assembled a panel of 17 voters to determine the best football movies of all time. Our top 10 mixes in hard-hitting dramas with lighthearted comedies.

Narrowing this list down to 10 was a ruthless task, which led to The Longest Yard , The Program and We Are Marshall just missing the cut. But just like when battling on the gridiron, some deserving movies inevitably had to fall short.

The story of Brian Piccolo was so inspirational that it didn't need much Hollywood dramatization. Brian's Song pretty much followed what happened in real life.

In 1967, the Chicago Bears began assigning road roommates by position. Running backs Brian Piccolo and Gale Sayers became the NFL's first interracial roommates.

The movie didn't focus too much on the scrutiny the players and coaches faced because Piccolo and Sayers roomed together. It focused more on their friendship and Piccolo helping Sayers recover from a major knee injury in 1968.

Piccolo was diagnosed with cancer in 1969, a devastating turn of events for Sayers and the entire Bears community. Piccolo died in 1970 at just 26 years old.

Piccolo's story has stuck with generations of football fans, but the movie isn't quite as memorable/rewatchable as the ones to come on this list.

The best plot point of Varsity Blues is the players, led by quarterback Jonathan "Mox" Moxon, standing up to abusive head coach Bud Kilmer.

The Coyotes going on to win the district championship game is secondary to the jerk coach losing the respect of his players and facing public shame for his actions.

Billy Bob is one of the most iconic football movie characters. It's anything but sunshine and rainbows for the enormous guard, who has a mental collapse, but he does get a happy ending by improbably scoring the game-winning touchdown.

Both Varsity Blues and Friday Night Lights depict the lives of high school football players in Texas, and both succeeded in their own ways. But as you'll see, our voters favored Friday Night Lights , in part because of its documentary style.

Above all, Little Giants is a fun movie. It's mostly lighthearted and makes you smile in a way few other sports movies do.

Who knows how many young girls Becky O'Shea has inspired by not only playing with the boys, but also getting the better of them.

The football scenes don't always hold up in terms of realism, but who doesn't love the creativity of "The Annexation of Puerto Rico" trick play that gives the Giants a game-winning 99-yard touchdown?

Rick Moranis and Ed O'Neill were perfectly cast as the O'Shea brothers. You know there are siblings like them all over America, and it was nice to see the smaller, less athletic one teach the bigger jock a lesson.

What makes Jerry Maguire a lock for these rankings is Cuba Gooding Jr.'s performance as Cardinals wide receiver Rod Tidwell. He won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor, which was well deserved.

Really, all scenes with Tidwell and Maguire (Tidwell's agent) were nearly flawless—with the " show me the money !" scene standing out—and the football scenes were high-quality as well.

While Jerry Maguire is one of the more critically acclaimed movies in these rankings, football itself is more of a subplot compared to the (problematic) love story between Maguire and Dorothy Boyd. The "you complete me" and "you had me at hello" quotes have embedded themselves into modern vernacular, but those don't help this film's ranking when evaluated strictly against other football movies.

The Waterboy is arguably the funniest football movie of all time—shoutout to Farmer Fran, who steals every scene he's in—but many of the football scenes hold up pretty well, too.

Coach Klein is in his bag in the second half of the Bourbon Bowl. Using Bobby Boucher as a lead blocker on a fake field goal, then following that up with a flea-flicker that had Boucher throwing to QB Gee Grenouille for the game-winning TD, was brilliant.

But what really makes the movie is Kathy Bates' portrayal of Helen "Mama" Boucher. Among her many great lines is: "That's nonsense. I invented electricity. Ben Franklin is the devil!"

Ultimately, The Waterboy had a capped ceiling in these rankings because several higher-ranked films drew on real-life stories that left viewers feeling more raw emotion. But it certainly has a special place in all our hearts, as do many of Adam Sandler's comedies from the 1990s.

The Replacements beats The Waterboy for the top spot among football comedies, though they aren't quite the same genre. The former has a more serious feel than the latter due to it being loosely based on the true story of the 1987 NFL strike.

In the movie, quarterback Shane Falco gets a career lifeline with the Washington Sentinels due to a players' strike. He vastly exceeds expectations, leading the team to within one win of a playoff berth.

Starting quarterback Eddie Martel returns for the final regular-season game and has a horrible first half, blaming the replacement players for his struggles.

Head coach Jimmy McGinty replaces Martel with Falco in the second half, and Falco leads a dramatic comeback in what will be the last chance many of his teammates will get in this top-end professional league with the players' strike ending.

Though the major plot points feel contrived, it's too endearing not to make this list. And it got a serious boost for the "I Will Survive" scene , one of the funniest in any sports movie.

What gives Any Given Sunday a different feel from most sports movies is the way the football scenes were filmed. It feels like you're experiencing the speed and violence firsthand.

And what makes it complicated to rank is how flawed Miami Sharks head coach Tony D'Amato and quarterback Willie Beamen are.

But that's on purpose. Any Given Sunday unapologetically portrays the seedy parts of the sport and its stars.

D'Amato's " game of inches " halftime speech is one of the best sports movie speeches of all time.

Ironically, Any Given Sunday was inches short of finishing second in our rankings. Fair or not, the fact that the movies in the Nos. 2 and 3 spots have more likable main characters might have been the difference.

Friday Night Lights captures the pressure and expectations of being a premier high school football team in Texas, often from the perspective of injured star running back Boobie Miles.

But head coach Gary Gaines' halftime speech from the state championship game might be what defines the movie.

"Can you live in that moment, as best you can, with clear eyes, love in your heart, joy in your heart?" Gaines asks. "If you can do that, gentlemen, you're perfect."

With Permian trailing by six and time for one more play, quarterback Mike Winchell scrambles and is tackled one yard short of the end zone.

It was a crushing loss for the Panthers, but they had no reason to hang their heads. They gave it their all, which made them perfect in Coach Gaines' view.

Rudy is the ultimate story about doing whatever it takes to fulfill a dream. It's based on the true story of Notre Dame walk-on Daniel "Rudy" Ruettiger.

In the movie, Rudy is promised that he'll suit up for one home game as a senior. But when the Fightin' Irish change coaches between his junior and senior seasons, that promise is nearly broken.

When Rudy is not on the dress list for the final home game, he quits the team. That sets up the most iconic quote of the movie.

"You're five-feet-nothin', 100-and-nothin', and you got hardly a speck of athletic ability," groundskeeper Fortune says to Rudy . "And you hung in with the best college football team in the land for two years. And you're also gonna walk out of here with a degree from the University of Notre Dame. In this lifetime, you don't have to prove nothin' to nobody except yourself."

Rudy returns to the team, and his teammates threaten to sit out unless he's allowed to dress for the finale, forcing the coach's hand. With the Irish routing Georgia Tech, Rudy takes the field for the final two plays, records a game-ending sack and is carried off by his teammates.

Rudy gets bonus points for its soundtrack, composed by Jerry Goldsmith. It's arguably the best sports movie soundtrack ever.

Remember the Titans will make you laugh. It will make you cry (RIP Gerry Bertier). It will make you want to run through a wall to play for Herman Boone and Bill Yoast. It will make you appreciate how human connection can make us look past our differences and change our worldview.

Yoast's speech —"You make sure they remember, forever, the night they played the Titans"—is one of the great speeches in sports movies. The "strong side, left side" scene between Bertier and Julius Campbell gives me goosebumps every time.

Denzel Washington gives an awe-inspiring performance that puts us in the shoes of Boone, who had to wear so many hats—football coach, life coach, husband, father—with a racist community ready to get him fired for any slip-up. In the movie, Boone navigated all of that to lead T.C. Williams to a perfect season, just as he did in real life during the 1971 season.

The football scenes mostly hold up well, save for the championship-winning trick play, which strains credibility given how many defenders are positioned deep to protect the end zone.

Despite that blemish, our voters chose Remember the Titans as the No. 1 football movie of all time in a landslide.

articles.title: 2027 UFL Draft Prospects Who Deserve Another Shot in the NFL
articles.summary: Football fans are fully focused on the NFL right now, but things are brewing in another professional league. While the 2027 UFL season won't kick off until late March, the latest UFL draft will begin with Rounds 1 and 2 on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Football fans are fully focused on the NFL right now, but things are brewing in another professional league. While the 2027 UFL season won't kick off until late March, the latest UFL draft will begin with Rounds 1 and 2 on Wednesday.

The Columbus Aviators will have the first overall pick and their choice of players from a pool of young NFL hopefuls.

The pool is open to players from the 2026 NFL draft class, as well as those from recent classes who were on an NFL roster after June 13 but who are currently unsigned. Many of those players could and probably should find their way back into the NFL in the not-too-distant future.

The list of former spring-ball players currently active in the NFL includes Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates, Minnesota Vikings defensive lineman Jalen Redmond, Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey and Denver Broncos linebacker Dondrea Tillman.

Here, we'll examine some of the top prospects from the UFL draft pool who deserve another NFL opportunity based on past production, positional value, skill set and projected upside.

Cornerback Beanie Bishop entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2024, signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The 26-year-old looked to be a long-term depth piece during his rookie season before spending most of 2025 on Pittsburgh's practice squad and ultimately being released.

He spent time with the New Orleans Saints and Chicago Bears this past offseason. In March, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reported that Bishop had been suspended for the first three games of the 2026 season for violating the NFL's substances of abuse policy. Chicago waived him with an injury settlement in late August.

The West Virginia product showed that he can play in the NFL during his time with the Steelers. He appeared in all 17 games with six starts in 2024 and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 59.5 in coverage.

While Bishop's size (5'10", 184 lbs) may force teams to view him as a slot-only corner, he should get the chance to rejuvenate his NFL stock in the spring.

Cornerback Cobee Bryant also entered the NFL as a free agent, joining the Atlanta Falcons in 2025. The 25-year-old appeared in seven games with one start for Atlanta as a rookie while bouncing between the active roster and the practice squad.

Bryant was waived by the Falcons in September.

While the Kansas product has a limited NFL resume ( 102 defensive snaps), he has the length to play on the perimeter (6'0", 180 lbs) and stood out at the East-West Shrine Bowl. He also flashed elite ball skills during his time in college.

In four seasons at Kansas, Bryant logged 22 passes defended, 13 interceptions, two fumble recoveries, and three defensive touchdowns.

NFL teams can almost never have too many experienced and versatile offensive linemen on the roster. While Darrian Dalcourt has never established himself as an NFL starter, he's gotten multiple opportunities to fill a depth role.

A 2024 undrafted free agent of the Baltimore Ravens, Dalcourt has also spent time with the Washington Commanders, Carolina Panthers, Cleveland Browns, and New England Patriots. However, he has never been moved from the practice squad to the active roster and was waived by New England in August.

While Dalcourt doesn't have regular-season experience in the NFL, he has spent time in several pro locker rooms after his five-year stint at Alabama. With the Crimson Tide, Dalcourt started games at both guard and center.

With solid size (6'3", 309 lbs), athleticism, and positional versatility, Dalcourt should see another NFL opportunity soon. If he adds some more starting experience in the UFL next year, he could become an intriguing potential bargain in the summer.

Ideal Offseason Landing Spots for NFL QB Reclamation Projects 🛬

There's plenty to like about safety Tanner McCalister, who entered the NFL as a 2023 undrafted free agent with the Browns.

The Oklahoma State and Ohio State product only appeared in three games with Cleveland in 2023 and three with the Denver Broncos in 2024. However, he has stood out enough to earn multiple stints with both Denver and the Kansas City Chiefs.

Released for the second time by Kansas City in September, McCalister should have the chance to earn more opportunities by standing out in the UFL. He has adequate size at 5'11" and 191 pounds, and he earned a solid 8.20 relative athletic score (RAS) entering the NFL.

McCalister was also a part of some huge games during his lone season with the Buckeyes.

In five collegiate seasons, McCalister recorded 149 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss, 13 passes defended, and four interceptions.

Tight end Tanner McLachlan has a chance to become an offensive force in the UFL, which would certainly earn him NFL attention. A 2024 sixth-round pick of the Cincinnati Bengals, he was also drafted into the CFL.

McLachlan appeared in just two games during his lone season in Cincinnati before being waived with an injury designation the following summer.

However, the physical traits that made him an intriguing NFL prospect—and earned him opportunities with the Los Angeles Chargers and San Francisco 49ers over the last two years—haven't dissipated.

The Arizona product is an athletic 6'5", 244-pound pass-catcher who broke Rob Gronkowski's school record for receptions. He ran a 4.61-second 40-yard dash at the scouting combine with a very impressive 9.39 RAS .

In two years at Arizona, McLachlan racked up 79 catches for 984 yards and six touchdowns.

Former San Diego State and California safety Patrick McMorris entered the NFL as a sixth-round pick of the Miami Dolphins in 2024.

The 6'0", 206-pound defensive back spent one season with the Dolphins before being waived as part of final cuts in 2025.

McMorris then spent time with the New York Giants and Arizona Cardinals in 2025 and joined San Francisco this past offseason before being waived in August. During his rookie season, he appeared in six games, playing almost exclusively on special teams.

What makes McMorris intriguing is his combination of size, physicality, and positional versatility. The 25-year-old played both free and strong safety in college and is capable of lining up in the slot. While he is a marginal athlete, he's a strong tackler with good instincts who had very good production in college.

In four seasons at San Diego State and one at Cal, McMorris tallied 252 total tackles, 11 tackles for loss, 23 passes defended, four fumble recoveries, and six interceptions.

Despite being a prolific college passer and a 2025 Heisman finalist, Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia went undrafted in the spring. He landed with the Baltimore Ravens as a free agent but was waived by July. No other NFL club has given him an opportunity since.

There are a couple of reasons why teams may be out on Pavia. The first is his size. At 5'10" and 207 pounds, he's below the normal NFL threshold for quarterbacks. Unlike the similarly sized Bryce Young and Dillon Gabriel, he isn't particularly polished as a processor.

Pavia also has a big, often brash personality that could raise concerns among teams considering him for a backup role.

However, Pavia didn't throw for 3,539 yards and 29 touchdowns last season by accident. He's a driven competitor, with solid physical tools, strong leadership skills, and a ton of experience.

Pavia should get a chance to start in the UFL, and if he can show some developmental progress and maturity in the coming spring, a few NFL teams should be willing to give him a look in the summer.

Linebacker Chris Paul Jr. didn't make the Los Angeles Rams' regular-season roster as a rookie in 2025, and though he quickly landed with the Seattle Seahawks, he never made it off of Seattle's practice squad.

The Seahawks waived Paul with an injury settlement in August.

However, the Ole Miss product was a promising draft prospect who excited the Rams enough to be taken in the fifth round.

"Paul's traits are worth betting on and he'd be a good fit as a WILL linebacker. It might take some time, but he can potentially become a quality starter in the NFL during his rookie contract and maybe even by year two," Matt Holder wrote for the Bleacher Report Scouting Department in 2025.

The 6'1", 228-pound Paul has 4.63 speed and more than enough upside to earn another chance in the NFL. While he couldn't stick with two of the league's better rosters, he has the skills to stand out in the UFL and earn himself more opportunities next summer.

We've seen a few professional kickers stick in the NFL after honing their skills in the UFL. Ben Sauls should get the chance to follow that trend, assuming he's selected in the draft.

The Pittsburgh product wasn't drafted into the NFL in 2025, though he did land with the Steelers as an undrafted free agent. He also spent time with Atlanta before getting the opportunity to kick in meaningful games for the Giants.

Sauls landed in New York last November, and he ended up kicking in three games. While he didn't attempt any kicks of over 50 yards, he made all eight of his field-goal attempts and all seven of his point-after tries last season.

This offseason, Sauls lost New York's kicking competition to rookie Dominic Zvada, and he was waived with an injury settlement in August. Given the NFL's lack of reliable kickers, Sauls deserves another shot, even if he's a rarity as a left-footed kicker.

We just saw running back/fullback Carson Steele in a pair of games for the Philadelphia Eagles last month. However, he suffered a dislocated shoulder and was subsequently released with an injury settlement.

Steele entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Chiefs in 2024. The 6'0", 228-pound ball-carrier spent two seasons in Kansas City and had a fairly substantial role during his rookie campaign. He finished the 2024 season with 183 rushing yards on 56 carries.

While Steele may not have the burst to be a quality NFL tailback, he has the combination of size, play strength, and vision to serve as a fullback or short-yardage specialist.

Between two seasons at Ball State and one at UCLA, Steele amassed 3,294 rushing yards, 486 receiving yards, and 30 combined touchdowns. If fully healthy, he could be one of the UFL's top rushers in 2027 and should parlay that into an NFL training camp spot.

Wide receiver Jamari Thrash was just waived by the Las Vegas Raiders in late October, and it wouldn't be a total shock to see some NFL teams show interest before he signs any agreement with the UFL.

A 2024 fifth-round pick out of Louisville, Thrash spent two seasons with the Browns and flashed solid NFL potential in limited action. The Louisville product caught 13 passes for 129 yards in 18 games with Cleveland. He suffered a leg injury this past summer, though, and was waived from injured reserve in September.

Thrash has a solid combination of size (6'0", 190 lbs), speed (4.46-second 40-yard dash), and route-running ability, which helped him to be highly productive in college.

In his final season at Georgia State, Thrash amassed 1,122 yards and seven touchdowns. He followed that campaign up with an 858-yard, six-touchdown season at Louisville.

NFL teams are almost always in the market for quality defensive tackles, which explains why the Jacksonville Jaguars acquired two of them—Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis—at the trade deadline.

Former UCLA standout Jay Toia doesn't have the upside or proven production of Davis or Godchaux, but he has an NFL-caliber blend of size (6'2", 340 lbs), play strength, and athleticism. He was a seventh-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 and appeared in five games as a rookie.

Toia has the tools needed to be a space-eating nose tackle in the NFL, though the Cowboys decided that he didn't fit the scheme of new defensive coordinator Christian Parker this past offseason. Toia was released in August and spent time on the Arizona Cardinals' practice squad before he was again waived last month.

In four seasons with the Bruins, Toia recorded 91 combined tackles, nine tackles for loss, three sacks, four passes defended, and a forced fumble.

articles.title: Week 11 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops Likely Available After Reviewing Box Scores
articles.summary: Week 11 is likely to be a tough week to navigate for many fantasy managers, which is unfortunate, as the fantasy playoffs are right around the corner. Injuries continue to make star players unavailable, and a deluge of bye weeks will further limit the player pool this week.
articles.body:
Week 11 is likely to be a tough week to navigate for many fantasy managers, which is unfortunate, as the fantasy playoffs are right around the corner. Injuries continue to make star players unavailable, and a deluge of bye weeks will further limit the player pool this week.

The Arizona Cardinals, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks have the week off.

Many managers will be scrambling to find fill-ins on the waiver wire in the coming days. Here, we'll examine some of the top options to target and play in Week 11, based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Cam Ward still hasn't established himself as a franchise quarterback for the Tennessee Titans. However, Tennessee has given him a bit more responsibility and freedom in recent weeks, which has led to some quality numbers.

Ward has only delivered one win this season, but he has thrown for at least 180 yards in each of his last three games. He has topped 20 fantasy points in each of his last two contests, and he should approach that number this week against the Dallas Cowboys.

The Cowboys can score points in bunches, meaning Tennessee will likely need to throw early and often. Dallas has also struggled defensively and has surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing QBs this season.

That all bodes well for Ward, who is rostered in only nine percent of fantasy leagues.

Samaje Perine is only a bit player in the Cincinnati Bengals' high-powered offense. However, he got some run on Sunday during Cincinnati's blowout win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He caught four passes, found the end zone, and finished with 13.9 fantasy points.

Perine should again approach double-digit fantasy points this week, as the Bengals look to attack a Washington Commanders defense that has been solid against the run. The Bengals have turned to Perine when starter Chase Brown has struggled before, giving him 14 carries in the Week 5 win over the Miami Dolphins.

The Bengals may also look to involve Perine as a receiver if the Commanders stifle their ground game. Given the fact that Cincinnati may build another big early lead on Monday night, Perine could see a heavy workload in the second half.

Perine is rostered in just 12 percent of fantasy leagues.

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

The Bengals' defense still isn't great, but it has started to tighten up against opposing passing games. Cincinnati has surrendered the 11th-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

Despite a less-than-ideal matchup, Commanders rookie receiver Antonio Williams is still an intriguing option in Week 11. Washington will need to rely on Jayden Daniels' arm to keep pace with the Bengals, and Williams has emerged as one of his top targets.

Since losing Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury, Williams and Stefon Diggs have become Daniels' go-to receivers. Williams has reached double-digit fantasy points in two of his last three games, and he has seen 15 targets in three games since Washington's bye.

Williams is still only rostered in 27 percent of fantasy leagues.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, TE, Washington Commanders

For managers dealing with players like Harold Fannin Jr., Kyle Pitts, Tucker Kraft, and Hunter Henry on bye, Chigoziem Okonkwo is an attractive alternative.

The Commanders tight end hasn't been a huge piece of the game plan, but he has seen an increase in targets over the past six weeks. He has topped double-digit fantasy points in three of his last five games and should have a solid floor against Cincinnati this week.

Given Washington's need to score points and Cincinnati's ability to slow opposing wideouts, Okonkwo should be targeted often. He saw eight targets in last week's win over the New York Giants, and that'll probably be his floor on Monday night.

The Bengals have surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season. Okonkwo is still only rostered in 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Inside Aaron Rodgers' unconventional life away from football, from his personal beliefs to his multi-million-dollar career
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is 42, in his 22nd NFL season and, by his own words, close to the end.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is 42, in his 22nd NFL season and, by his own words, close to the end. The Steelers quarterback signed a one-year deal for 2026 with $22 million guaranteed and up to $25 million with incentives. He then told reporters, “This is it.” The story that keeps readers curious sits outside the stadium: a darkness retreat, a venture fund, a long State Farm partnership and a marriage he kept quiet until a ring gave it away.Aaron Rodgers’ life away from football is more layered than his imageAaron Rodgers has spent his career acting like the odd one out. He fell to 24th in the 2005 draft, waited behind Brett Favre, then won four MVP awards and a Super Bowl. That early sting seems to have stayed with him. Ever since, he has trusted his own judgment over the room’s.You can see it in his career moves. He left Green Bay for the Jets in 2023. He joined Pittsburgh in 2025 on a deal worth $13.65 million, a bargain for a four-time MVP. He threw for 3,322 yards and 24 touchdowns that year, and the Steelers’ season ended in the wild-card round against Houston. Then he came back for more, at a higher salary.Green Bay still pulls at him. Early in 2023, after what looked like his last game as a Packer, he said on The Pat McAfee Show: “Eighteen years, man. That’s always going to be home.” This August he opened his final season with a preseason game against the Packers and told reporters he wished it were being played in Green Bay. Hard edges, soft spot. That mix explains much of what follows.The darkness retreat, plant medicine and a vaccine row that followed himFew quarterbacks would announce a four-day darkness retreat while deciding whether to play again. Rodgers did, and it went viral within days. The idea is simple. You sit alone in a lightless room, with no screens and no distractions. He treated it as a way to think about what came next. The internet treated it as a punchline.He has also spoken openly about plant medicine such as ayahuasca. I am not offering a verdict on any of it. What stands out is that he talks about these experiences in public, on a show with a huge audience, knowing the jokes are coming.The 2021 vaccine episode cost him more. In August of that year he told reporters he was “immunized.” It later became clear he meant a non-vaccine approach, not the shot most teams were pushing. He tested positive that November and missed a game. Critics said a star with his reach should have been plainer about it. Supporters saw an adult making a personal call. Both views fit the record.The pattern is consistent. Rodgers treats his own life like a long experiment and accepts the bruises that come with sharing the results.How Aaron Rodgers built a business life that does not depend on a contractLook past the quarterback and you find a careful businessman. His State Farm partnership dates back to 2013, which in endorsement terms is a lifetime. Most athletes rotate sponsors every few years. Rodgers kept one going for over a decade, and the “Discount Double Check” ads made him a comic figure far beyond Wisconsin.The bigger move came in 2019, when he co-founded Rx3 Ventures with Nate Raabe and Byron Roth. The fund started at $50 million and focuses on consumer brands. Early bets included the rowing machine maker Hydrow, helmet company VICIS and Privé Revaux eyewear, with cheques of roughly $1 million to $3 million.Add his regular spot on The Pat McAfee Show, and you see the shape of it. Football gives him the platform. Media, investing and sponsorships give him income that does not rise and fall with a single contract. That matters at his age. A one-year deal at $22 million is real money, but it is smaller than what he earned at his peak. His wider business keeps him from needing the next big offer.The private marriage and a quieter, family-minded RodgersFor a man who talks about almost everything, Rodgers has guarded one subject well. On December 23, 2024, he mentioned a girlfriend named Brittani on McAfee’s show while explaining a late Christmas package. He added with a smile: “Not Britney Spears, no, this is Brittani with an ‘i.’” That was nearly all the public learned for months.In May 2025, people noticed a dark band on his hand at a Kentucky Derby event. On June 10, at Steelers minicamp, he settled it. “Yeah, it’s a wedding ring,” he said, adding that he had been married for a couple of months. He later said the two eloped. Brittani stays off social media, and Rodgers has said she prefers it that way.The shift is bigger than the secret. In an interview with Sports Illustrated that summer, he credited his wife with helping him become more open to repairing relationships with his estranged family. For a player long defined by distance, that is a notable change in tone.Meanwhile, the football clock keeps running. The Steelers faced the Bengals on November 15, and local coverage called his opening stretch the worst start of his career. The season is far from finished, and so is Rodgers’ own explanation of how he wants it to end.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: CJ Carr, Sellers, Mensah to Falcons, Browns, Vikings in New 2027 NFL Mock Draft from ESPN's Reid
articles.summary: The New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns and Minnesota Vikings are all predicted to target quarterbacks in the first round of the 2027 NFL draft in the latest mock from ESPN's Jordan Reid.
articles.body:
The New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns and Minnesota Vikings are all predicted to target quarterbacks in the first round of the 2027 NFL draft in the latest mock from ESPN's Jordan Reid .

Reid predicted the Jets will start out the run by trading up to No. 2 and selecting Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker.

He projects the Falcons selecting Notre Dame's CJ Carr at No. 8 before the Browns take South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers at No. 17 and the Vikings finish out the round by snagging Miami's Darian Mensah at No. 29.

Ideal Offseason Landing Spots for NFL QB Reclamation Projects 🛬

Reid described Carr as a "more mobile Kirk Cousins" who could potentially find immediate success in place of Michael Penix Jr. thanks to other Falcons stars like Bijan Robinson and Drake London.

In Cleveland, Sellers would be stepping in for Deshaun Watson, who is playing this season in the final year of a contract that was largely disastrous for the Browns.

Even if Watson ends up re-signing in Cleveland, the Browns could still want to add another option at quarterback, although Reid noted Sellers is "still a bit polarizing for NFL scouts... but the league values his athletic tools."

"I could see a team such as the Browns, who have two first-round picks, taking a chance on him at this point of Round 1," Reid reported.

Another team with a veteran quarterback on an expiring contract is the Vikings, which brought Cousins back ahead of the deadline but could lose both him and Kyler Murray to free agency this summer.

After the Vikings gave up on their most recent first-round quarterback selection by trading J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants, Reid speculated Mensah "would provide a stable floor at the position for the Vikings" despite scouts describing him as not having as high of a ceiling as other draft candidates.

Some other notable quarterbacks including Oregon's Dante Moore and Texas' Arch Manning did not end up in Reid's projected first round.

Both signal callers were featured in Bleacher Report's latest first-round mock draft , which featured three top-10 quarterback picks as the Dolphins target Mestemaker at No. 3, the Jets take Manning at No. 4 and the Arizona Cardinals acquire Mensah at No. 9.

B/R scouts predict Moore will go to the Browns at No. 16 before the Philadelphia Eagles trade up to draft Sellers at No. 25 and the Pittsburgh Steelers select Carr at No. 26.

How these quarterbacks perform down the stretch of the season during potential College Football Playoff runs could further shift the outlook of the 2027 class by the time the draft kicks off next April in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: Arch Manning Out, Jets Trade for QB Mestemaker in New 2027 NFL Mock Draft from ESPN's Jordan Reid
articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning's polarizing 2026 season has seen his draft stock plummet.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning's polarizing 2026 season has seen his draft stock plummet.

ESPN's Jordan Reid released his latest 2027 NFL mock draft on Wednesday, and Manning wasn't included in any of the 32 first-round selections, four of which were quarterbacks.

Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker was the first signal-caller off the board in a mock trade between the Los Angeles Chargers and the New York Jets, who own three 2027 first-round picks following 2025 trades with the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys. Reid predicted that the Jets would package their No. 4 pick, the Cowboys' No. 13 pick and a 2028 third-round pick to move up to select their quarterback of the future while holding on to the Colts' No. 6 pick.

The full top 10 from Reid's latest mock draft is as follows:

Tennessee Titans: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

New York Jets (via projected trade with LAC): Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

Miami Dolphins: Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

Los Angeles Chargers (via projected trade with NYJ): Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

Philadelphia Eagles: Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

New York Jets (via IND): Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Arizona Cardinals: Jordan Seaton, OT, USC

Atlanta Falcons: CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame

Houston Texans: Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah

New Orleans Saints: Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

Manning was once projected as a future No. 1 draft pick, but he hasn't performed at that level this year. The youngster has thrown for 2,198 yards, 19 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while completing 64.7 percent of his passes. In this past Saturday's win over LSU, he threw a game-winning touchdown in the fourth quarter, but that came after he threw three interceptions.

Reid isn't the only evaluator who has lost faith in Manning. However, in the latest mock draft from B/R's NFL Scouting Department, he was still projected to be selected fourth overall by the Jets.

Meanwhile, Mestemaker has skyrocketed up draft boards throughout the season for his steady play in his first year with the Cowboys after transferring from North Texas. He's thrown for 3,239 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while completing 66.4 percent of his passes.

The 2027 draft class will be loaded with talent, but it will be crucial for teams like the Jets to make the right selections if they hope to rise from the bottom of the NFL.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza's Pros & Cons from 1st Career Start Dissected by NFL Insiders in New Raiders Rumors
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza may have given the Las Vegas Raiders hope he could be their quarterback of the future despite struggling against Devon Witherspoon on the blitz in last Sunday's loss to the visiting Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza may have given the Las Vegas Raiders hope he could be their quarterback of the future despite struggling against Devon Witherspoon on the blitz in last Sunday's loss to the visiting Seattle Seahawks.

ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler reported people around the league saw positive aspects to Mendoza's game when he made his first NFL start in place of Kirk Cousins during a 21-13 loss to the defending Super Bowl champions.

"He clearly offers something with his legs that Kirk Cousins does not at this point, and he made throws outside the numbers that people view as a sign the offense can evolve with him at the helm," Graziano noted.

Fowler agreed: "People I spoke with saw flashes."

According to Graziano and Fowler, one NFC offensive coach said Mendoza "is a good fit for Klint [Kubiak's] offense."

"I thought he did well when facing live bullets," the coach told Graziano and Fowler.

Both Graziano and Fowler noted, however, Mendoza could use work on his reads and his tactics against the pass rush. The Raiders got off to a 10-7 start before a second-quarter blitz led by Witherspoon sparked a strong back half from the Seahawks' defense.

"The Seahawks eventually overwhelmed him. He missed a few blitzes and took six sacks. He missed some throws, particularly to the left side of the field," Fowler reported.

"But as one personnel evaluator noted, the game didn't look too big for him and he kept his eyes downfield, whether in the pocket or on the move. The arm strength and mobility are obvious."

Mendoza finished his debut as the Raiders' starter having going 17-for-29 with 143 passing yards to go along with six carries for 22 rushing yards and a touchdown.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said after the loss he felt blitz-heavy defense "is just something that you're going to see as a rookie quarterback."

"When they're blitzing, then they're going to be short in coverage, so that's a chance for us to make big plays," Kubiak said Tuesday. "You want teams to blitz you."

The Raiders will hope Mendoza will have more answers in his second NFL start should the Denver Broncos decide to lean on the same tactic after Sunday's matchup kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET in Colorado.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill Visits Usain Bolt's Doctor in New Video amid as WR Eyes NFL Comeback from Major Injury
articles.summary: Amid his attempt to return to NFL action, wide receiver Tyreek Hill recently visited a German doctor who is famous in the sports world.
articles.body:
Amid his attempt to return to NFL action, wide receiver Tyreek Hill recently visited a German doctor who is famous in the sports world.

In a video posted on his YouTube channel, Hill documented a trip to Germany that saw him work with Dr. Hans-Wilhelm Müller-Wohlfahrt, who is known for treating legendary athletes such as Olympic sprinter Usain Bolt, NBA icons Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant, and soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo:

The video description noted that during his visit, Hill "underwent specialized treatments and rehabilitation sessions, with a holistic, hands-on approach to sports medicine; the week focused on understanding his body as a whole, addressing the complexities of his injury, and taking intentional steps toward a stronger, healthier return to the field."

After battling through a wrist injury for much of the 2024 season with the Miami Dolphins, Hill was limited to just four games last season due to a torn ACL.

The Dolphins released Hill in February, and he went unsigned throughout the offseason, and still has yet to sign with a new team.

Hill has posted plenty of workout videos over the past several months, though, showcasing his progress and push toward resuming his NFL career.

In September, Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus appeared on the Pat McAfee Show (h/t Kyle Dvorchak of NBC Sports) and said multiple teams had inquired about potentially signing him.

At the time, Rosenhaus noted that Hill could return to game action "perhaps some time in October."

However, October has come and gone without any movement, as the 32-year-old Hill remains a free agent.

That doesn't mean Hill playing in 2026 is out of the question, though, as he may very well be the best option for receiver-needy teams now that the trade deadline has passed.

An eight-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and one-time Super Bowl champion over 10 seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs and Dolphins, Hill has been one of the best and most dynamic wideouts of the past decade.

For his career, Hill has recorded 819 receptions for 11,363 yards and 83 touchdowns, and he isn't too far removed from back-to-back seasons with over 1,700 receiving yards in 2022 and 2023.

There is plenty of uncertainty regarding whether Hill can recapture his past magic, but he seems to be doing everything possible physically to get back on the field and be a contributor for an NFL team.

articles.title: Christian Parker will reportedly remain Cowboys' defensive coordinator, but play-calling duties handed to Mike Pettine
articles.summary: Pettine was hired in October as a senior defensive assistant.
articles.body:
Christian Parker's job as Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator is safe for now, but he will reportedly no longer be calling the plays, according to ESPN's Todd Archer and Kimberly A. Martin .

Mike Pettine, who was added last month as a senior defensive assistant to support Parker, will have play-calling responsibilities going forward.

The decision comes after another poor showing by the Dallas defense during Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't exactly show support for the 34-year-old Parker, who was hired in the offseason after two seasons on Nick Sirianni's staff with the Philadelphia Eagles.

"At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," Scottenheimer said after the 49ers recorded 584 yards of offense, the most the Cowboys have allowed at home in franchise history.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones expressed some support for the young defensive coordinator, while also pointing to winnable close games as an issue.

"It's what it is. He's a young coach, it's his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say you would hope you'd win games like the last that we've lost," Jones said, via The Athletic's Jon Machota . "I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."

During his his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, Jones didn't say change was coming, but did acknowledge that Parker's position has been discussed.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here," Jones said. "But we are talking about those things."

Through 10 weeks, the Cowboys' defense is 32nd in total yards allowed (393.8 per game) and rushing yards allowed (154.1 pg), 31st in points allowed (28.2 pg) and has the third-fewest takeaways (8), including only four interceptions.

It's not just a 2026 season issue, either. The Cowboys have allowed opponents to score at least 20 points in each of their last 17 games, dating back to Week 12 of last season. Dallas finished 30th in total defense last season and allowed 511 points, which resulted in the firing of Parker's predecessor, Matt Eberflus.

articles.title: Cowboys Make Major Change to Defense, Latest NFL Rumors on DC Christian Parker & Mike Pettine
articles.summary: After a historically bad defensive performance in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Dallas Cowboys are making a change at play-caller on that side of the ball.
articles.body:
After a historically bad defensive performance in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Dallas Cowboys are making a change at play-caller on that side of the ball.

Per ESPN's Kimberley Martin, Adam Schefter and Todd Archer , Christian Parker will remain defensive coordinator with senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine taking over play-calling duties for the Cowboys.

This move comes after Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan's Shan & RJ radio show they were discussing potential changes to their defensive staff while being mum about the details.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said.

Parker's status was a primary talking point coming out of the loss to San Francisco. The Cowboys allowed season-highs in points (46), total yards (584) and rushing yards (210).

The 584 yards allowed were the most Dallas has ever given up in a home game. San Francisco also became the first team since the 2000 St. Louis Rams to have three 65-plus yard touchdowns in a game.

Even though Sunday's game put a spotlight on Parker and the defense, the Cowboys have struggled on that side of the ball all season. They rank 28th in success rate, 30th in points allowed per game and last in EPA per play.

The Cowboys expected to be better on defense after a disastrous 2025 because they would have a full season with Quinnen Williams, traded for Rashan Gary and used their first three picks in the 2026 draft on defenders, including Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence in the first round.

Instead, this unit has been roughly the same as the 2025 group. Parker, who is the youngest defensive coordinator in franchise history at 34 years old, was named to the role after spending the previous two seasons working on Nick Siranni's staff with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Pettine joined the Cowboys staff in the offseason to provide support for Parker as a first-time defensive coordinator. The 60-year-old has worked in the NFL every year since 2002, including two years as a head coach with the Cleveland Browns from 2014 to '15.

The Cowboys will look to rebound on Sunday when they host the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium.

articles.title: From first prom date to expecting fourth baby: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes love story is straight out of a movie
articles.summary: When we talk about Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ epic love story, Hannah Montana’s “If We Were a Movie” song comes to mind.
articles.body: When we talk about Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ epic love story, Hannah Montana’s “If We Were a Movie” song comes to mind.The lyrics go: “If we were a movie, you’d be the right guy. And I’d be the best friend that you’d fall in love with. In the end, we’d be laughing, watching the sunset. Fade to black, show the names, play the happy song.”Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ love story was tested by distancePatrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes [nee Lynne Matthews]’ love story began as two friends in Texas who went to school together.They became close in 2011, when Patrick was a freshman at Whitehouse High School. They began dating when he was in 10th grade, and she was in 11th grade at Whitehouse High School in Texas.They attended the school prom as a couple in 2013. Patrick captioned his Instagram prom photo, “Best prom date a guy could ask for!! #prom2013 #bestfriend #greatnight.” Brittany graduated from Whitehouse in 2013 while Patrick graduated in 2014. Brittany [Aug. 31, 1995] is weeks older than Patrick [September 17, 1995].Their love story was tested by distance when they attended universities 400 miles apart. He played football at Texas Tech University while she was into soccer at the University of Texas at Tyler.Brittany was often found cheering for Patrick from the sidelines when their schedules allowed. “He ended up going to Texas Tech, and that’s when it really hit me, ‘Oh, sh*t, he might go play professional football,” Brittany told TODAY in Dec. 2020.“It was surreal to see him living his dream, and seeing him grow as an athlete and as a man in general was amazing.”In 2017, Brittany played for the professional soccer team UMF Afturelding/Fram in Iceland. That same year, Patrick was drafted into the NFL to play for the Kansas City Chiefs. That same year, Matthews retired from soccer, and moved to Kansas City, where she became a certified fitness trainer.She later launched Brittany Lynne Fitness, which offers access to different fitness programs designed by Matthews. In a 2019 interview with Yahoo Sports, Patrick credited Brittany with being a positive influence on his diet and nutrition.“Eating-wise, I’m blessed that my girlfriend is [big on] nutrition, so she helps me out with that - she’s [about] fitness,” Patrick said.“I just try to eliminate some of the bad meals, the fast food, the foods that aren’t great for your body and don’t help you get the most out of it. I’m a picky eater, but I still try to eat healthy stuff like chicken, salmon, and all the [other] stuff I like a lot.”Patrick Mahomes’ proposal to Brittany MahomesIn February 2020, the Kansas City Chiefs won the Super Bowl. Brittany and Patrick made headlines with their iconic pose - hug lift or jump-and-hug-lift. Patrick lifted Brittany in his arms while she wrapped her arms and legs around him.That same year in September, Patrick popped the heart-fluttering question: “Will you marry me?” The quarterback told 610 Radio that proposing to Brittany made him more nervous than playing in the Super Bowl.“Probably proposing, I would say. You don’t think it’s going to be nerve-wracking, especially when you’ve been with someone for so long, but before you get on that knee, your heart’s racing, I promise you that,” he told the Kansas City, Missouri radio show.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ dogs Steel and SilverIn 2016, the couple adopted a puppy named Steel to celebrate Valentine’s Day. Brittany grew up cheering for the Pittsburgh Steelers, so they named the puppy Steel. “I’ll take a puppy over flowers and candy any day,” Brittany captioned her Instagram post then.Steel is a full-grown pit bull today. They also have a second dog, a Cane Corso, named Silver. Silver entered their lives in 2019.Steel and Silver inspired the names of their children - Sterling Skye, Bronze, and Golden Raye. Their incoming fourth child is a baby boy, and fans are already speculating that the couple could name him Titan[ium], Copper, Nickel, Chrome, Mercury, and more.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ children and KC CurrentIn early September came the heart-fluttering proposal; in late September came the pregnancy announcement! In October 2020, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes painted their dogs’ paws pink to reveal the baby’s gender! February 20, 2021, first baby girl and first child Sterling Skye Mahomes was born.A year and a month later, in March 2022, the NFL power couple got married in Maui, Hawaii, surrounded by friends and family. Their 1-year-old daughter, Sterling Skye, was the flower girl at their wedding.Two months later in May, they announced they were expecting their second baby. That same year, in November [11.28.2022], their second child and first baby boy, Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III, was born.In January 2023, Patrick joined Brittany in business as co-owner of the Kansas City Current, a women’s soccer team that is now worth $325 million! Her name continues the couple’s metallic naming tradition - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden. In March 2026, the couple celebrated their fourth wedding anniversary.A few months later, in November 2026, the NFL’s most loved couple announced they were expecting their fourth child and second baby boy. Surrounded by immediate family, the couple cut a white cake with blue cream on the inside.Brittany and Patrick Mahomes’ fourth baby gender revealHolding their three babies, Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 1, Brittany and Patrick Mahomes inserted inverted empty champagne glasses into the white cake. When they took out their glasses, the glasses were filled with blue cream and white cake.Brittany jumped with excitement while Patrick looked at Brittany to give her another peck! Along with the announcement, Kansas City Current colored confetti dropped from the ceiling! Teal and silver.Patrick’s mother, Randi Mahomes, hugged Brittany’s mother, Diana Massey. The three kids played on the ground with the teal-and-silver confetti.Brittany and Patrick Mahomes now enter the Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce and Matthew Stafford and Kelly Stafford club - with four kids. Just that, Kylie and Kelly both have four girls each; Brittany, on the other hand, has two girls and one boy, and is expecting another boy! So, two boys and two girls- two of each is the best!Patrick and Brittany’s love story is nothing short of a movie. There’s already several books on Mahomes. articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still searching for answers on defense, but it doesn't sound like they're considering any coaching changes for now.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are still searching for answers on defense, but it doesn't sound like they're considering any coaching changes for now.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that "it feels like everything is on the table" regarding Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker's status. However, after speaking to sources in Dallas, Fowler noted that "they believe firing coaches wouldn't solve much."

The Cowboys still decided to adjust Parker's responsibilities, as ESPN's Todd Archer and Kimberley A. Martin reported on Wednesday that senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will now call the defense on game days. Parker will retain his title as the team's defensive coordinator.

Report: Cowboys DC Stripped of Playcalling

Parker, who is in his first year on the Cowboys' coaching staff, hasn't been able to turn around the disappointing unit. After ranking 30th in the NFL in 2025 with 377.0 yards allowed per game, Dallas ranks last in the league this year with an average of 393.8 yards allowed.

Fowler pointed out that Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer and owner Jerry Jones "have been noncommittal about Parker, so perhaps change is on the table soon." Pettine was viewed as "a natural replacement" for Parker, who had worked under him when he was the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator.

"Parker is a good young coach. It just hasn't worked out thus far," Fowler stated. "The personnel on defense, though improved on paper from a year ago, still isn't great and is clearly a year away. ... Plus, it's tough to make wholesale changes, in part because Dallas is very much alive in a weak NFC East."

The Cowboys (4-6) will try to start moving in the right direction when they face the Tennessee Titans (1-8) on Sunday.

articles.title: Latest on Drake Maye's Contract, Patriots Future After Major Injury on Hit from Aidan Hutchinson
articles.summary: The potentially season-ending injury Drake Maye suffered after a 5-5 start to the 2026 season may have raised some questions about his long-term future with the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
The potentially season-ending injury Drake Maye suffered after a 5-5 start to the 2026 season may have raised some questions about his long-term future with the New England Patriots.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that long-term questions for the franchise includes "do the Patriots pay Maye, who's eligible for an extension?"

"Most likely, yes, but both parties are not exactly entering the offseason with momentum," Fowler concluded.

Maye is currently signed through 2027 with a 2028 club option on his rookie contract. He is eligible for an extension after the 2027 campaign.

After leading the Patriots to Super Bowl LX, Maye struggled early in his third NFL season.

Maye completed a career-low 65.6 percent of his passes for 2,330 yards, 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions before he went down last Sunday with an ankle injury that NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported could sideline him for the rest of the campaign.

He had made 43 consecutive starts prior to the injury, good for the third-longest active streak in the NFL, per ESPN's Mike Reiss .

Maye is currently playing under a cap hit of less than $10 million, while the top eight quarterbacks in the NFL have all signed deals worth at least $55 million per year, per Over the Cap . The Kansas City Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes set the league's all-time record in June with a deal worth an average of $64 million per year.

Should the Patriots decide to wait on an extension, and should Maye enjoy a resurgence next season, the price to re-sign him before he potentially hits free agency in 2028 might balloon even higher.

Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf will need to decide if last year's playoff run is enough motivation to re-sign Maye this summer even if his ankle injury might mean the team won't see him play again until 2027.

articles.title: Cowboys demote defensive coordinator Christian Parker, give play-calling duties to more experienced coach
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys handed defensive play-calling duties to Mike Pettine after Christian Parker's unit gave up the most yards, with his future in question.
articles.body: Note to NFL defensive coordinators: You give up more yards than any other team, you give up 30 points three times and 46 points once by mid-November, you're in trouble, and Christian Parker found that out on Wednesday. The Dallas Cowboys demoted Parker, their first-year defensive coordinator, stripping him of play-calling duties. COWBOYS' ELIJAH GARCIA GETS COMPLETELY FOOLED ON 49ERS' TRICK PLAY, UNDERSCORING POOR DEFENSIVE EFFORT IN LOSS And while Parker is not fired and retains his title, his future with the club beyond this year is clearly in question, according to a league source. The Cowboys, meanwhile, are handing the defensive play-calling duties to Mike Pettine. Pettine, 60, joined the club five weeks ago to lend his opinions and experience based on the fact he has pieced together a good resume as an experienced NFL defensive coordinator. Over his decades-long coaching career, Pettine's NFL highlights include serving as the defensive coordinator for the New York Jets from 2009 to 2012, when his aggressive units helped reach back-to-back AFC Championship games. He orchestrated successful turnarounds as coordinator for the Buffalo Bills in 2013 and the Green Bay Packers from 2018 to 2020. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The expectation is that Pettine will make some general adjustments to the Cowboys defense but an all-out rebranding of the unit is not expected. COWBOYS DEFENSIVE COORDINATOR SHOWS WHY HE SHOULD BE FIRED BY ASKING VON MILLER TO COVER CHRISTIAN MCCAFFREY ON A PASS PLAY One thing seems certain as Pettine calls the Dallas defense going forward: There will not be a moment in which he asks 37-year-old edge linebacker Von Miller to cover a speedy running back or wide receiver down the field. One-on-one, no less. That happened in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
