articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk, Jayden Daniels 'Reconciled' After WR's Comments, New NFL Rumors Amid 49ers Return
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk have reportedly buried the hatchet in the months since Aiyuk made critical comments regarding Daniels over the summer.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk have reportedly buried the hatchet in the months since Aiyuk made critical comments regarding Daniels over the summer.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the former Arizona State University teammates have "reconciled," as Aiyuk reached out to Daniels "about a month ago" to talk things out.

Aiyuk, who has not played an NFL game since October 2024, was placed on the reserve/left squad list by the 49ers last season.

In the months that followed, he lobbied for the opportunity to join forces with Daniels in Washington, but when that didn't happen, he started to take shots at the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year.

Back in July, disparaged Daniels in a video on his Instagram stories , saying, "You gonna have to stop running behind your momma, and I might believe what you talkin' bout."

Aiyuk was finally reinstated by the NFL last week, opening the door for him to potentially return to game action as soon as this season.

The 49ers were subsequently granted a two-game roster exemption, which expires on Nov. 23 following the team's Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings.

At that point, the Niners will have to make a decision on what to do with Aiyuk, whether that is keeping him and placing him on the 53-man roster or releasing him.

Given that 49ers general manager John Lynch told reporters in January that Aiyuk had "played his last snap" with the 49ers, cutting Aiyuk seems to be the most likely resolution.

Should that happen, it is fair to wonder if Washington would be an option for Aiyuk, especially since No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin is out for the rest of the season due to injury.

Fowler noted that while he is "not sure" what the chances are of Aiyuk joining the Commanders, Aiyuk and Daniels are "good again," which perhaps makes it a more likely scenario.

When Daniels and Aiyuk were teammates at Arizona State in 2019, they had a great connection, as Aiyuk finished with 65 receptions for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns en route to San Francisco selecting him 25th overall in the 2020 NFL draft.

Aiyuk went on to enjoy some productive seasons with the 49ers, including topping 1,000 receiving yards in back-to-back seasons in 2022 and 2023.

Although they are only 3-5-1, the Commanders are just two games behind the New York Giants for the NFC East lead, so adding a player with Aiyuk's ability may be something the organization at least considers for the stretch run.

articles.title: Special camps at booths highlight gaps in voter verification
articles.summary: Ek Aur Avsar camp in Ranchi revealed voter verification gaps in SIR claims phase, with pending cases due to missing documents, absent voters and poor outreach.
articles.body: Ranchi: Wednesday’s ‘Ek Aur Avsar’ (one more opportunity) camp at a Ranchi school exposed gaps in voter verification during the claims and objections phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with residents struggling to clear objections and booth level officers reporting missing documents, absent voters and poor response.For Shafique Ansari of Tharpakhna, the camp was another attempt to get his daughter-in-law, Suhana Parween, enrolled as a voter. Ansari said his son, Jawed Akhtar, married Suhana, a resident of Karbala Chowk, in Aug 2025. She applied as a new voter and her name appeared in the draft roll, but was placed in the ‘no-mapping’ category as her details could not be linked to her parents’ names in the 2003 electoral roll.Ansari said Suhana’s parents’ names were not on the voter list, though her grandparents’ names were. The family submitted those details under Election Commission guidelines, but the objection remained unresolved.An ECI official said the case involved a missing link between Suhana and her parents or grandparents. “She is unable to provide documents or proof of her place and date of birth in India,” the official said. The family also obtained a certificate signed by the ward 18 councillor and neighbours confirming that Suhana was Jawed’s wife. “Parental linkage is required as per ECI guidelines,” the official said.BLOs said several verification cases were still pending. Sunita Devi, BLO at booth 301 in Tharpakhna, said 10 of 616 voters still had verification-related work pending, mainly because of missing documents. At booth 306, Sunita Lakra said 16 of 623 voters remained unresolved. The cases included people living abroad, those who had shifted and those unable to submit documents.At booth 519 in Khoratoli, BLO Sahina Khatun said 10 of around 600 voters had been marked absent, but only one had attended the camp. Clara Gari, BLO at booth 515, said many voters remained unavailable or uncooperative, while incorrect phone numbers made it difficult to contact them. “The ERO will take a decision by passing a speaking order in these cases,” she said.Chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar inspected polling stations and visited homes of voters listed under ASDD and those who had failed to submit documents despite two notices. He said door-to-door verification and a reasoned speaking order by the electoral registration officer were mandatory before declaring any voter ineligible and deleting the name from the draft roll.Kumar found the verification process unsatisfactory, saying officials had not made adequate efforts to contact voters and collect documents.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Predicting how the NFC North will finish with 4 great teams
articles.summary: Four brilliant teams, but only one can win.
articles.body:
It's a really bad year to be a good team in the NFC North. While the majority of the NFL's divisions have settled into a football bell curve of the good, fine, and bad — the North is stacked with four of the league's best teams fighting over three playoff spots down the stretch. Someone is going to win, cementing themselves as a true contender in the NFC, two teams will likely secure wild-card spots, becoming the most dangerous non-winners in the playoffs, and one team is going to finish with a 10+ win record and have nothing to show for it.

We're hurtling towards another season where one fanbase decries the NFL's playoff format. The only question that remains is: Who? The Bears, Lions, Packers, and Vikings all have incredible characteristics in their own right, but diving into trends, remaining schedule, and future potential, there's a likely way we're going to see this play out.

Current record: 7-2 Remaining SoS (lower is better): +14.7 Future opponents: Saints, Lions, Jaguars, Dolphins, Bills, Packers, Lions, Vikings Projected finish: 12-5

The Bears are so much fun to watch. Boasting a Top 10 offense and defense in scoring/scoring allowed, the complete revitalization of this football team by Ben Johnson is almost complete in just his second year at the helm.

Caleb Williams took another step forward in his development this season, though it hasn't always been perfect. A hamstring injury forced him to miss three games, and his overall performance has been excellent on paper, but there's a key element to his game that's still missing: Red Zone efficiency. Moving the football between the 20s hasn't been a problem for Williams this season, but it's clear that Johnson still doesn't fully trust his young QB in short-field situations, favoring a shift to the run game over asking him to make tight throws.

This has resulted in him being on pace for an injury-adjusted 23 passing touchdowns this season, which puts him around 16th in the NFL in passing TDs, much closer to the Bo Nix/Geno Smith caliber of QB than the league's elite. Bears fans shouldn't take this as a knock on Williams, but rather an exciting development for the future. We are still yet to see Caleb be fully unlocked, and he's already on pace to lead this team to the playoffs. I have no doubt the Bears coaching staff can round out his game and make him even better.

When it comes to the remaining schedule, the Bears boast the toughest remaining slate in the NFC North. They have enough ability to win the majority of their remaining games, but not quite enough to take the division outright. The x-factor down the stretch will be Jeffrey Simmons. One of the best acquisitions around the trade deadline , Chicago got a massive boost to their defense with the interior pass rusher, who has been fantastic since his arrival. If Simmons is capable of disrupting key drives then there's a real chance the Bears could flip another loss to a win down the stretch.

Current record: 7-2 Remaining SoS (lower is better): +2.8 Future opponents: Buccaneers, Bears, Falcons, Titans, Vikings, Giants, Bears, Packers Projected finish: 13-4

"Undeniable" is the best adjective for the Lions offense this season. Working off the inverse of most offensive principles, Detroit uses Jared Goff as their chain-mover and red zone scoring threat, while Jahmyr Gibbs' rushing ability delivers the explosive plays. This has been incredibly difficult for opponents to deal with, as the Lions are poised to be the only team in the NFL to finish with a QB over 4,500 yards passing and a running back with over 1,500 yards rushing

If you can sense the "but" coming, you'd be right. Detroit's offense has been incredible, but the defense is another story entirely. The injury bug has bitten this team big time, with its two most important players all out for the remainder of the season in LB Jack Campbell, and now DE Aidan Hutchinson, who hurt himself in Week 10.

Before these injuries, a banged-up secondary was struggling, meaning things are only going to get worse for Detroit defensively from here. This team ranks 15th in the NFL in points allowed and 28th against the pass. These are scary metrics for a team poised to hit the playoffs and face some of the league's best quarterbacks. The saving grace here is that the remaining schedule looks great for them, with only the Vikings and Bears looking like real challenges at this point.

This is a team that will get a high wild card seed, likely win a playoff game, but major questions remain about whether their defense has enough to stop the best teams in the league.

Current record: 6-4 Remaining SoS (lower is better): +12.0 Future opponents: Rams, Saints, Bills, Dolphins, Bears, Texans, Lions Projected finish: 10-7

It's been a weird year for the Green Bay Packers. Full of ups and downs, the Packers have shown they can rise to beat some of the NFL's best teams, but also lose inexplicably to the likes of the Falcons, and be pushed to overtime by the Jets. This leaves us with a team that is very good, but just feels a step behind everyone else in the NFC North right now.

Jordan Love and the Packers' passing game are fascinatingly weird. This is a unit that never makes things easy on themselves, opting to generate as many explosive deep passes through the air as possible, in a very feast-or-famine playstyle. At times this has been incredible, typified by their blowout win over the Bears in Week 5 — but also looked sophomoric and unsophisticated against the Vikings in Week 10.

When we get down to brass tacks, there are just too many points of failure for Green Bay this season. The running game has been atrocious, the defense has been middling, and above all else it's tough to discern what the identity of this football team is. They're good at a lot of things, but not great at anything in particular. That's ultimately what will put them on the outside looking in when the playoffs roll around, especially in light of a difficult schedule down the stretch.

Current record: 7-2 Remaining SoS (lower is better): -5.9 Future opponents: 49ers, Falcons, Panthers, Patriots, Lions, Commanders, Jets, Bears Projected finish: 14-3

It's impossible to heap any more praise on the Minnesota defense. Watch this team play one game and you immediately understand how special this unit is. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has steadily improved his players from the moment he arrived, with 2026 being the crescendo of his brilliance — orchestrating a group of guys who aren't household names, and transforming them into a group of monsters.

There have been some standout performances in Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel, but overall this isn't a team you'd characterize as being full of elite talent on defense. The only thing holding them back was an absolutely putrid offense, which was led by two horrible quarterbacks in Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.

That all changed at the NFL trade deadline when the Vikings re-acquired Kirk Cousins for their playoff push. The impact was immediately noticeable, with Cousins being simply good enough to allow the defense to swallow the Packers, and ultimately deliver the win.

Minnesota is in an incredible spot right now where they not only have momentum behind them, but the easiest remaining schedule in the NFC North. The only game they're not favored in to close out the season is against the 49ers, which could quite easily be a win, depending on how the defense is able to stop Brock Purdy's quick passing game.

It's beginning to feel like the Vikings' division to lose, with the stars aligning for them. As for the playoffs? We'll need to wait and see. As brilliant as this team could be, there's also a weight of baggage and history pressuring them to perform. It's unclear if this team is ready to rise to the moment.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys make Mike Pettine the defensive play caller, Christian Parker is now DC in name only
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys, who have been laying the ground for a change since Sunday’s totally unacceptable and historically inept performance in the 46-40 loss to...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys , who have been laying the ground for a change since Sunday's totally unacceptable and historically inept performance in the 46-40 loss to the Green Bay Packers, have officially stripped the play calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Per sources, Mike Pettine, a long-time NFL defensive coordinator, will take over as the play caller on defense. Parker will keep his title as defensive coordinator but Pettine will make the calls on game day, starting Sunday against the Tennessee Titans.

This moment was likely inevitable when Pettine was hired last month to serve as a senior consultant to Parker following a disastrous start to the season for the first-time coordinator.

Never mind that Pettine was considered a Parker mentor who had given him his first job in the NFL at Green Bay back in 2019 or that the Cowboys tried to hire him last February to serve as an advisor when they initially hired Parker.

Pettine spent eight years as an NFL defensive coordinator and two as head coach of the Cleveland Browns.

Pettine turned them down in the spring and they had to talk him off vacation and in Italy with his wife to come help rescue a Cowboys defense under Parker that was already trending as one of the worst in the NFL.

That he reported to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and not Pettine was the first sign that this alignment was not in Parker's favor, while giving the Cowboys an option if they needed to make a change.

Giving up a whopping 584 yards against the 49ers, the most in a home game in team history and the third most ever for the franchise, proved to be final straw.

The loss to the 49ers featured three touchdowns of 66 yards or more.

But the Cowboys have allowed six plays of at least 50 yards over the last three games and a league-high eight all season.

Pettine has been here for the last five games. And while the sacks have increased with 17 of the 22 on the season coming since he showed up, the overall ineptitude remains.

All totaled, the Cowboys are last in NFL in yards, run defense and third-down defense. They are 26th in pass defense and 30th in scoring defense. They have had trouble against the pass, getting to the quarterback, tackling and getting off the field all season.

Will Pettine calling plays make that much of a difference?

The Cowboys hope so. At 4-5, they still have hope of getting back into the NFC East playoff chase, trailing the first-place New York Giants, who are 5-3-1.

Considering the offense, led by quarterback Dak Prescott ranks fifth in points and eighth in yards and third in passing yards, they likely only need to get marginally better on defense.

They certainly have a chance to build some confidence and gain some momentum in the two weeks with games against 1-8 Titans on Sunday followed by the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles four days later on Thanksgiving Day. The Eagles are riding a seven-game losing streak.

The Cowboys will then get 11 days off before playing at the Seattle Seahawks on Dec. 7.

articles.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams on gauntlet of NFC North race
articles.summary: Caleb Williams discussed the pressure of the Bears' tough NFC North playoff race after dropping from first to third during their bye week.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have been on a roll in Ben Johnson's second season as head coach, where they're riding a four-game winning streak and have lost just two games this season. Unfortunately, they also happen to play in the NFC North, which has been historically good this season.

After their win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Minnesota Vikings' loss in Week 9, Chicago went into their bye week first in the NFC North. However, after the Vikings and Detroit Lions won in blowout fashion in Week 10, the Bears are now third in the division despite not playing. At 7-2, Chicago is the No. 6 seed in the NFC and every team in the division is currently in the playoffs.

From the outside, it seems like there is a lot of pressure on the Bears to keep winning, especially after starting 0-2 in the division. However, quarterback Caleb Williams does not feel that pressure as Chicago is focusing on going 1-0 each week.

Photos from the Bears' ugly 27-24 win over Bucs in Week 9

"The pressure idea, I don't think we have that here inside the building," Williams said. "I think that's the biggest thing, is us understanding it only matters what we think, what we feel. You know, one week we could be Super Bowl contenders. One week we could be playoff contenders. One week we could be wild card contenders, one week we could be the worst team in the league. And that comes from the outside noise and all of that.

"But for us inside, we think - I mean, I would say we know who we are. We're confident in who we are, in what we're building and what we're going for. And so, with that, we've got to just keep focused on being 1-0 each week, and then that whole pressure idea goes away each week with doing that."

The Green Bay Packers are on bye for Week 11, so they will not be able to make a move in the division. However, the Bears are facing the 3-6 New Orleans Saints, which is a very winnable game. The Detroit Lions are facing the Buccaneers, which is a game they can win. But the Vikings are facing the San Francisco 49ers, who are the No. 1 seed in the NFC.

Therefore, Chicago has the chance to move into the No. 1 or No. 2 seed in the division depending on the results of their games and the Lions' and Vikings' games.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: Jets 3-round mock draft update
articles.summary: In our latest mock draft update for the Jets, we go three rounds and get a franchise quarterback in the first round.
articles.body:
Of all the bad teams in the NFL this season, the one with the best chance to turn things around in the offseason is the New York Jets. Thanks to some big trades, New York is currently sitting on three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. This time around, we aim for as many playmakers as possible and work to rebuild the offense first where the team has struggled for years.

Here's our updated three-round mock draft for the Jets.

First round - QB Drew Mestemaker - Oklahoma State

Mestemaker has separated himself from the other top quarterbacks in this draft with a strong first season at Oklahoma State. The Jets have been searching for their franchise quarterback and Mestemaker might just be that guy.

First round - CB Leonard Moore - Notre Dame

The Jets traded away Sauce Gardner and get his replacement in an upgrade with Notre Dame's Leonard Moore.

First round - WR Charlie Becker - Indiana

It's crazy to think how good Charlie Becker would be if Indiana had better quarterback play because he's a complete weapon in the passing game and just a notch below Jeremiah Smith.

Second round - DT Xavier Gilliam - Tennessee

Gilliam is a fast-rising prospect as he puts together one of the best seasons in college football. He provides a great blend of run stuffing and pass rusher on the interior.

Third round - S Brauntae Johnson - Notre Dame

The Jets go back to Notre Dame in the third for another defensive back. Johnson has a chance to keep climbing draft boards and might be out of reach here.

articles.title: Former 3-Year Cincinnati Bengals Player Signs With Chiefs After Release
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals and Kansas City Chiefs both hold 7-2 records and will face off in just a few weeks at Paycor Stadium. On Wednesday, the Bengals saw on...
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Kansas City Chiefs both hold 7-2 records and will face off in just a few weeks at Paycor Stadium.

On Wednesday, the Bengals saw one of their former players sign with the Chiefs as an unrestricted free agent.

Fred Johnson is currently in his eighth NFL season. He began his career with the Bengals from 2019-2021 before spending the last four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Eagles, however, decided to waive him following the trade deadline during their bye week. Johnson cleared waivers on Nov. 16, making him free to sign elsewhere.

Ultimately, Kansas City is looking for some reliable depth up front, which is something Johnson has provided during his eight seasons in the league.

Via ESPN's Ian Rapoport : "The #Chiefs are signing former #Eagles OT Fred Johnson to their practice squad and he'll likely be elevated to the 53-man roster."

Johnson went undrafted in 2019 and initially signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers, but Pittsburgh waived him in early October, allowing the Bengals to claim him.

He went on to appear in 23 games during his time in the Queen City and started eight games for Cincinnati. Johnson played for the Bengals just before the franchise began to find success with star quarterback Joe Burrow.

Following his departure from the Bengals, Johnson spent one season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022 before eventually signing with the Eagles in 2023. He went on to win a Super Bowl with the organization.

He appeared in 58 games during his time in Philadelphia and made 14 starts, none of which came this season.

articles.title: Skip Bayless says there’s already something he really doesn’t like about Arch Manning
articles.summary: Skip Bayless has mixed feelings on what he’s been seeing from Arch Manning. There are big expectations on the shoulders of the 22-year-old due to his family’...
articles.body:
Skip Bayless has mixed feelings on what he's been seeing from Arch Manning.

There are big expectations on the shoulders of the 22-year-old due to his family's track record of producing NFL quarterbacks.

It's for this reason that Bayless says he's watched every game that Manning has played, though he still finds himself conflicted on the Texas Longhorns star.

Skip Bayless argues Arch Manning has all the talent but an attitude issue

On a recent episode of Gridiron , Skip Bayless said that after watching every Arch Manning game, there are moments that you get excited each time.

The Texas Longhorns quarterback will produce, according to Bayless, four or five throws per game that live up to his surname and justify his potential.

He even went as far as to say that he believes Manning is even more talented in terms of his overall game than the three members of his family that played quarterback in the NFL, Archie, Peyton, and Eli Manning.

However, for all of the positives that Bayless can see, he also believes that, in his words, "the intangibles are scarily lacking."

"He gets overemotional," Bayless argued. "He's thin-skinned. He quickly gets down on himself. He loses his poise under fire quickly. But, he'll get it back because he knows he's a Manning. He knows what runs through his bloodline."

The veteran commentator also believes that he's seen examples of Manning having "some spoiled brat in him."

He particularly took issue with the way the young quarterback has become "really defensive" with the media at times, saying, "I don't like the way he handles himself in interviews now."

Bayless believes that with how talented Manning is, even if there are some inconsistencies to his game, he should let this do the talking.

articles.title: NFL news: 4 QBs picked in 1st round of new ESPN mock draft, but Arch Manning isn’t 1 of them

articles.body:
Arch Manning entered the 2026 college football season with expectations of becoming the next No. 1 overall NFL Draft pick. However, Texas' star quarterback is conspicuously absent from the first round of ESPN analyst Jordan Reid's latest 2027 mock draft. Instead, four other quarterbacks are projected to hear their names called on Day 1. This reflects Manning's uneven season and the rising stock of several intriguing alternatives.

Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker headlines the group at No. 2. The New York Jets are projected to acquire the pick through a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers. Notre Dame's CJ Carr follows at No. 8 to Atlanta. That's where Reid sees him as a potential successor to Michael Penix Jr. Reid even compares his playing style to a more mobile Kirk Cousins. At No. 17, South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers lands with Cleveland through the Los Angeles Rams' selection. He offers a potential long-term answer beyond Deshaun Watson. Miami's Darian Mensah rounds out the quartet at No. 29. Minnesota potentially views him as a future replacement for Cousins.

Manning's omission is particularly notable given his preseason billing. The 6-foot-4 Texas quarterback has thrown for 2,198 yards and 19 touchdowns through 10 games. He has helped the Longhorns reach an 8–2 record. However, 10 interceptions, mechanical inconsistencies, and struggles under pressure have cooled his draft stock. His impressive arm talent and mobility remain attractive traits. That said, evaluators still have questions about his consistency. Manning has yet to decide whether to enter the 2027 draft or return to Austin. That leaves his eventual draft position uncertain.

articles.body:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot.

Burrow lit up the Steelers during a 38-18 win that extended Cincinnati's winning streak to five games. Burrow was 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the victory.

The four touchdowns moved him up to 20 over the course of the winning streak and he leads the league with 27 touchdown passes over the entire season.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that Burrow has been named the AFC offensive player of the week. It's the second time he's won that prize this season and the 10th time in his career.
